title: 1,000 Places to See Before You Die
author: Patricia Schultz
description: This original bucket list contains a wide variety of stunning places around the globe! A must-have in every globetrotter's library, even if it's purely aspirational.

author: Stephen King
description: A time-traveling splendour from the King. What would you do if you had the opportunity to change history for the better? A chilling political journey into the United States' past, with King's usual wit.

title: 1st to Die
author: James Patterson
description: This thrilling first book in the Women's Murder Club series takes four crime-solving friends through a classic murder mystery. Will they make it through the twists this case has in store for them?

title: The 7 Stages of Grieving
author: Wesley Enoch & Deborah Mailman
description: A powerful one-woman play about an Aboriginal woman delivering a series of direct-address monologues and poems connecting the recent death of her Nana with the larger cycles of oppression and grief caused by Australia's colonial history and racist present.

title: 84, Charing Cross Road
author: Helene Hanff
description: An epistolary memoir about a friendship that develops over a shared love of books. A lighthearted, humorous collection of letters between a bookseller in London and a writer in New York City, desperate to fill gaps in her collection.

title: A Dance With Dragons
author: George R. R. Martin
description: Who would have thought that the fifth tome in the ASOIAF series has even more dragons, complex politics, and mysterious betrayals in store for us than ever before? Also, George, if you read this: Winds of Winter when?!

title: A Deepness in the Sky
author: Vernor Vinge
description: An interstellar trade conflict unfolds between two rivalling powers in this epic and thought-provoking sci-fi prequel. A dramatic modern classic of speculative sci-fi!

title: Design Patterns; Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
author: E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson, J. Vlissides
description: The classic reference for object-oriented programming, written by the legendary Gang of Four: a catalogue of reusable solutions to that solve common problems and make your code cleaner, reusable, and future-proof

title: A Dictionary of the English Language
author: Samuel Johnson
description: I've heard the 1740s were a good decade for the English language. Check out lots of words and their meanings in this slightly outdated collection.

title: A Fire Upon the Deep
author: Vernor Vinge
description: Buckle up for an epic space adventure that kicks off the Zones of Thought series and introduces a mind-bending future thousands of years from now.
qualities: Age Rating Mature [customers do not accept this as fantasy]

title: A Fire Upon the Deep
author: James Lovegrove & Nancy Holder
description: This book series continues the story of the Serenity's Crew we never got to see in the TV series. Bounty hunters, hired criminals, mysterious research labs, brown coats, homey spaceships, allies, enemies, laughter, and drama... This space western has it all!

title: A Game of Thrones
author: George R. R. Martin
description: Stern lords, ambitious ladies, rising queens, and underestimated bastards. This book kicks off an epic fantasy saga full of tragedy, twists, and undead. Winter is coming, and so is the drama!

title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
author: Holly Jackson
description: Everyone in her small town believes the case to be solved. But when young Pippa starts digging up the details of a murder from years past for her final school project, she discovers secrets yet untold.

title: A Room of One's Own
author: Virginia Woolf
description: This classic piece by Virginia Woolf is both a thought-provoking essay and a narrative exploration of the position of women as characters, as well as writers, in a literary tradition dominated by the patriarchy.

title: Rosalind Franklin; The Dark Lady of DNA
author: Brenda Maddox
description: Rosalind Franklin's contribution to one of the greatest discoveries of the 20th century wasn't acknowledged during her lifetime. This is an excellent biography of the woman whose research was crucial in determining the structure of DNA.

title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
description: From atoms to galaxies, this popular science book takes readers on a wild journey through the past, uncovering the secrets of our fascinating universe. For all of those readers out there who are interested in nearly everything.

title: A Storm of Swords
author: George R. R. Martin
description: War still wages in the Seven Kingdoms, the lands of the ASOIAF fantasy series. Alliances are made just as quickly as they are broken. And don't even get me started on the weddings.

title: A Study in Scarlet
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: In this first appearance of the eccentric detective Sherlock Holmes and his partner Dr Watson, the pair take out the old magnifying glass to solve a murder case in Victorian London.

title: A Time to Kill
author: John Grisham
description: In this tragic legal drama by John Grisham, set in a fictional county of 1980s Mississippi, the young attorney Jake Brigance attempts to let justice prevail even in a world full of racial injustice.

title: A Wrinkle in Time
author: Madeleine L'Engle
description: This "science fantasy" adventure starts off the classic Time Quintet series where three young heroes travel through time and space and face matters of good and evil.

title: ABCC; A Bookstonbury Crochet Collection
author: Various Authors
description: Crochet your favourite Bookstonian icons and create your own pocket-sized version of our beautiful town! 120 easy-to-follow and cosy patterns, such as: St Bookston, Raw Fish, Seagull, Mobile Bookshop, Dog, Plants, and many more!

title: Abridgment of Murray's English Grammar
author: Lindley Murray
description: Grammar is entirely made up! It can't hurt you! But, since most of us have to practise it anyway, why not make it fun with this early nineteenth-century American school guide?

title: Ace; What Asexuality Reveals About Desire, Society and the Meaning of Sex
author: Angela Chen
description: What does it mean to be asexual? Reimagine human connection by exploring intersections of identity, sexuality and culture through a collection of critiques, reflections and conversations with community.

title: The Acts of King Arthur and His Noble Knights
author: John Steinbeck
description: This adaptation of Malory's Morte d'Arthur (The Death of King Arthur) was published after the author's death. Steinbeck tried using modern language within the frame of Middle English. Proving yet again that authors with weird fixations write the most interesting books.

title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn; Adventures of Tom and Huck #2
author: Mark Twain
description: Mark Twain shows us the hypocrisy of 19th century Mississippi through the dawning understanding of a young boy's conscience. From the evils of slavery to toxic masculinity, Huck has to reckon with what he sees and decide for himself. And it takes him a while...

title: After the Funeral
author: Agatha Christie
description: Usually, death precedes a funeral. But with this English family, things go awry quickly, and only Detective Poirot can help them find out who dun did it now.

title: Alanna; The First Adventure (The Song of the Lioness #1)
author: Tamora Pierce
description: Alanna disguises herself as a boy to become a knight - but keeping that secret in between combat training, dealing with her magical Gift, making friends (and enemies!), and growing up is a tall order in this foundational youth fantasy work.

title: Alias Grace
author: Margaret Atwood
description: In this narrativised version of a historical murder case, a young woman's crimes come into question when she is released from prison. Is Grace Marks really a killer?

title: Alvar Aalto
author: Alvar Aalto
description: Get to know the Finnish design master Alvar Aalto, as this book takes us on a visual journey through almost sixty years of iconic creations, including photographs, plans, and sketches.

title: Amadeus
author: Peter Shaffer
description: Salieri's dreams of becoming history's best composer are threatened when childish upstart Mozart wows Vienna with his musical genius. Can Salieri ruin Mozart's career in time? A play about ambition, treachery, and the lengths one will go for fame.

title: American Psycho
author: Bret Easton Ellis
description: American Psycho details the increasingly dark and violent stream-of-consciousness of a young, rich, narcissistic yuppie working on Wall Street in 90s Manhattan. Contains graphic descriptions of gore and violence.

title: Among the Hidden; (The Shadow Children #1)
author: Margaret Peterson Haddix
description: As the third child in his family, Luke's very existence is forbidden. When he meets another forbidden child, can the pair execute a dangerous plan to escape the shadows? The first in the dystopian Shadow Children series.

title: Anathem
author: Neal Stephenson
description: What happens when all of the planet's intellectuals are shut off from the rest of the world, left to ponder existence without ever experiencing it? Find out in this epic and ambitious sci-fi page-turner.

title: Ancillary Justice; Imperial Radch #1
author: Ann Leckie
description: What would you do if you were a giant spaceship controlling hundreds of soldiers, now betrayed and trapped in one fragile body? If you're like Breq, you'd take revenge on the colonial empire that made you?

title: And The World Spins Anyway
author: Georgie Jones
description: In the author's debut collection of poetry and short stories, she invites readers to take a step away from social media and feel a little less alone in this chaotic, beautiful world. A refreshing and relatable read.

title: Angels & Demons
author: Dan Brown
description: The first in a series of thrilling mystery novels, Angels & Demons entails an elaborate assassination plot on high-ranking Vatican officials. But what did the mysterious Illuminati have to do with it all?

title: Angels in America; A Gay Fantasia on National Themes
author: Tony Kushner
description: A play so long it's traditionally shown over two consecutive days, Angels in America explores the 1980's American AIDS crisis in a surrealist deconstruction of religion and sexual identity.

title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
description: The allegorical tale of anthropomorphic farm animals, who overthrow the farmer's rule over them and attempt to lead the farm themselves. It is one of the most important pieces of 20th-century political satire, asking: What happens after the revolution?

title: The Animals of Farthing Wood
author: Colin Dann
description: The book behind a TV series that traumatized an entire generation recounts the journey of Fox, Badger, Mole and the other inhabitants of Farthing Wood as they strike out trying to find a new home. Their heart-breaking story continues in a further six books.

title: Annabel Lee
author: Edgar Allen Poe
description: Poe's verses shines beautifully in this haunting and tragic tale of forbidden love. Annabel Lee us a classic poem which immerses the reader in an eerie atmosphere and makes them long for a ghostly girl.

title: Architecture in Britain; 1530-1830
author: John N. Summerson
description: From the Renaissance to Neoclassicism, this guide charts the development of English architectural theory and practice, alongside marvellous colour photographs by A.F. Kersting.

title: Ariel
author: Sylvia Plath
description: A collection of poems, some tender, some despairing, some nihilistic, and so much more. Written in the last three years before Plath's death and published posthumously.

title: Arnheim's Principles of Athletic Training; A Competency-Based Approach
author: William E. Prentice
description: This book is so competency-based, you'll be diagnosing old injuries in everyone you see and testing range of motion on yourself constantly. Learn how to treat sprained ankles, wrap a bandage, and other helpful training tips for the average athlete. Possibly outdated!

title: Around the World in Eighty Days
author: Jules Verne
description: When an eccentric Englishman's unwavering punctuality is questioned, he wagers that he can circumnavigate the world in only 80 days, and we follow his almost impossible journey.

title: Art of the Modern Movie Poster; International Postwar Style and Design
author: Various Authors
description: A lovely collection of over 1,500 vintage film posters, perfect for any film buff, poster-collector, or owner of a coffee table.

title: Artemis Fowl
author: Eoin Colfer
description: When criminally inclined teenager Artemis tries to restore his family's fortune, he accidentally messes with the wrong fairies. Suddenly, he finds himself amidst a folk of high-tech fae.

title: As Good As Dead
author: Holly Jackson
description: The finale to the Good Girl's Guide to Murder YA series and a catching mystery for any true crime podcast fans out there. Will our titular Good Girl make it out unscathed?

title: Ashfall Legacy; Ashfall #1
author: Pittacus Lore
description: Syd Chambers, alien-human hybrid, has never known his father, a Denza native who disappeared years ago. Picking up the trail, Syd now journeys beyond Earth to seek out his father, discovering a universe-shattering secret along the way.

title: Assassin's Apprentice; The Farseer Trilogy Book One
author: Robin Hobb
description: Fitz was born out of wedlock to the crown prince, and for that, he is hated. Join Fitz as he learns the politics and intrigue of the palace whilst being raised in the stables. Does he have a touch of the Farseer magic that is so vied for by the royal family?

title: Asterios Polyp
author: David Mazzucchelli
description: Asterios is one of the world's greatest architects. This award-winning graphic novel follows how the rigid lines of his personality and architectural style shatter, sending him on an aimless journey that transforms a once self-absorbed man into someone who cares.

title: At the Earth's Core
author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
description: The Hollow Earth sci-fi novel for anyone who read 1864's Journey to the Centre of the Earth and thought: "Not enough dinosaurs!"

title: Atmosphere
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description: Joan Goodwin has always loved the stars. When she’s selected for NASA’s new astronaut programme, she finds friendship, purpose, and a love she never expected. But one mission will change everything.

title: Attack On Titan; Volume 1
author: Hajime Isayama
description: Eren Yeager has sworn to take revenge on the giant humanoid creatures known as Titans, who destroyed his home and killed his mother. An action-packed and thrilling first volume of the dystopian fantasy manga.

title: Babel; or the Necessity of Violence
author: R. F. Kuang
description: This novel explores an alternate-reality British Empire, in which languages and their meanings are harnessed for their immense magical power.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
description: An unrivalled piece of gothic historical fiction by Toni Morrison, a master of magical realism. Beloved tells a story about the trauma of slavery and how past hurt can linger like a ghost.

title: Better Than the Movies
author: Lynn Painter
description: Liz is on a quest for a teen love story like in the movies. Can her annoying neighbour Wes really help her go to prom with her crush? And why does he have to be so attractive?

title: Call Me by Your Name
author: André Aciman
description: Their big age gap seems to be unable to deter Elio and Oliver from their obsession with each other, and they experience the highs and lows of a gay summer romance in 1980s Italy.

title: Camp Damascus
author: Chuck Tingle
description: Rose has started receiving demonic visions and coughing up swarms of flies. Her investigations into why keep leading her to the gay conversion camp run by her Christian community. But she's never been there before—or has she?

title: Can't Spell Treason Without Tea; Tomes and Tea #1
author: Rebecca Thorne
description: Come along with Reyna and Kianthe as they escape the clutches of cruel queens and mage obligations in order to open their dream bookshop and tea salon. Watch as the two women fall even more in love and slowly find their place in the world. And what's this about dragons?

title: Cat's Eye
author: Margaret Atwood
description: Cat's Eye tells the tale of a woman's art, memory, and a childhood friendship gone awry. How can she come to terms with her past?

title: Catcher in the Rye, The
author: JD Salinger
description: Holden Caulfield thinks you're a phony. A disaffected teenager travels around 1950's New York City after he's expelled from school. A literary classic with pages of casually-written monologues lamenting alienation, depression, and the inauthenticity of adults.

title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
author: Roald Dahl
description: Only five lucky winners of a golden ticket will be allowed to discover the true goings-on in Willy Wonka's magical chocolate factory. Join them in this illustrated children's tale.

title: Charlotte's Web
author: E. B. White
description: When a clever spider and a radiant pig become friends, what could stand in their way? A charming children's classic with beautiful illustrations.

title: Chemical Chaos; Horrible Science
author: Nick Arnold & Tony De Saulles
description: Chemistry is confusing, and chemistry lessons are boring. Fret not! For this book is not about the bits you learn in school—but the funny bits, the fascinating bits and the bits that end up in blasts and bangs and dodgy discoveries!

title: Charmed Life; (Chrestomanci, Book 1)
author: Diana Wynne Jones
description: In the first of the Chrestomanci Series we meet Eric 'Cat' Chant. After the death of his parents, he and his sister move into Chrestomanci Castle to live with the world's most powerful enchanter and his family. Things, however, aren't quote what they appear to be.

title: Chemistry; The Central Science
author: Theodore L. Brown
description: An essential guide for all students looking to expand their knowledge of the sciences. This classic textbook contains all the essentials to begin understanding the squishiest of all sciences.

title: The Chicago Manual of Style (CMOS)
author: University of Chicago Press
description: Are you playing pin-the-hyphen with your sentences? Currently lost in a forest of commas? Worry no more, with 200+ pages of writing rules for publications, in this vintage style guide used by academics and (some) trade publishers!

title: A Child's Garden of Verses
author: Robert Louis Stevenson & Tasha Tudor
description: A collection of sixty-six poems for imaginative children, accompanied by the gentle watercolour illustrations of Tasha Tudor.

title: Children of Time; (Book 1)
author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
description: An experiment into accelerated evolution on a terraformed planet was thwarted, but evolution still finds a way. Even on a planet lightyears away, this series presents our society with a mirror when it shows us the problems of a different species. Arachnophobes beware!

title: Chocolat; Book 1
author: Joanne Harris
description: Vianne's new chocolaterie is a refuge for the over-looked townspeople of Lansquenet. Customers are given a mug of bittersweet hot chocolate, a sympathetic ear, and just a touch of magic-much to the disapproval of the local priest.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
description: You might know her story already, as Odysseus tells it. But in this modern retelling of Greek mythology, the tale of the sorceress on her island gains a whole new depth.

title: Clap When You Land
author: Elizabeth Acevedo
description: Yahaira has lost her father, her hero. Camino has lost her father, a near stranger. Both have gained a sister. In this powerful story written in verse, two girls learn to grieve and dream together.

title: Cleopatra and Frankenstein
author: Coco Mellors
description: A whirlwind marriage between a young painter and a wealthy older man reshapes the lives of everyone around them. Funny, messy, and moving, this novel explores love, identity, friendship, and the strange ways we grow up.

title: Collected Poems; 1934-1952
author: Dylan Thomas
description: One of the most important Welsh poets of the 20th century, Thomas' writing is lauded for its strong imagery and thought-provoking depths. Recommended reading for the seaside!

title: Confess
author: Colleen Hoover
description: As Auburn is trying to rebuild her life, she is instantly smitten with the mysterious artist Owen. But can their relationship last as his past is revealed? A suspenseful adult romance unfolds.

title: Conversations with Friends
author: Sally Rooney
description: This novel follows Frances as she navigates the complex relationships with her best friend and ex-girlfriend, Bobbi, and an older married couple, Nick and Melissa. A piercing exploration of blurred boundaries of intimacy and the struggles of one's identity.

title: Dark Age; (Red Rising #5)
author: Pierce Brown
description: The war for the solar system continues. When peace has a different meaning to everyone, what does it mean to be a hero? This violent space opera is packed with political intrigue. Whose army will prove itself victorious? And what does victory look like in this truly Dark Age?

title: The Dark is Rising
author: Susan Cooper
description: Following a terrifying night, Will wakes on his 11th birthday to a world covered in snow and a world changed. Will learns that he is one of the Old Ones and joins the battle against the Dark. Second in a classic fantasy series for kids.

title: Dark Matter
author: Blake Crouch
description: A thrilling action plot unfolds when ordinary physics professor Jason is abducted and finds himself in a parallel world. What dark paths will he face to make it back to his old life?

title: Dark Places
author: Gillian Flynn
description: Little Libby's life in rural Kansas is forever changed when she witnesses the murder of her family. Twenty-four years later, she revisits it all for the entertainment of crime-loving strangers.

title: The Dark Portal; Book One of The Deptford Mice
author: Robin Jarvis
description: No one has ever seen Jupiter, the living god worshipped by rats living below Deptford. In this dark fantasy, Audrey, a young mouse, ventures into the sewers where she discovers her missing father was last seen in Jupiter's altar chamber. A thrilling read for kids.

title: Death in Yellowstone; Accidents and Foolhardiness in the First National Park
author: Lee H. Whittlesey
description: Grizzly bear attacks, hot springs, and avalanches, oh my ! Cautionary tales about what not to do in one of America's wildest national parks.

title: Death Note; Volume 1
author: Tsugumi Ohba
description: When the power over life and death falls into the hands of Light Yagami, the young student vows to use it for good. But death god Ryuk might have other plans.

title: Death of a Salesman; Certain Private Conversations in Two Acts and a Requiem
author: Arthur Miller
description: It's 1940 and Willy Loman is as fatally insecure as his career. This depressing play asks whether the pursuit of the consumerist American dream is really all it's cracked up to be.

title: Death on the Nile
author: Agatha Christie
description: Detective Poirot is keeping to the background on his Egyptian vacation to carefully observe the mystery unfolding before him. Everyone had a motive, but who is cold-blooded enough to be the killer?

title: Divergent
author: Veronica Roth
description: In a post-apocalyptic Chicago, sixteen-year-old Tris is left with no choice but to join one of five factions. Prepare for an action-packed, dystopian story for young adult readers.

title: Down Under
author: Bill Bryson
description: An entertaining yet educational travelogue exploring a Sunburned Country , also known as Australia. Marvel about the country's people, history, landscape, flora and fauna.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: A chilling classic that masterfully mixes the 19th-century epistolary novel with early gothic horror. It follows boring businessman Jonathan Harker on a trip to a certain Transylvanian castle...

title: Dragonsong
author: Anne McCaffrey
description: Menolly can't stay in her fishing village, which forbids her dreams and confines her to rigid gender roles. Surprisingly, the new life awaiting her holds songs and dragons in store.

title: Dreamer's Pool; Blackthorn & Grim #1
author: Juliet Marillier
description: Two new friends start new lives after a magical escape. Blackthorn is a healer, Grim does physical labor. The duo's work on a local crime draws the Prince's attention. He needs their help with a problem of his own. A fantasy trilogy with slow-burn romance!

title: The Dry; (Aaron Falk #1)
author: Jane Harper
description: Police investigator Aaron Falk returns home for the funeral of his friend in the small Australian town that shunned him years ago. In this outback mystery, Falk uncovers not just how his friend died, but how it's connected to the crime he was framed for years ago.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
description: In this comedy of manners from Austen, socialite Emma is very confident in her matchmaking skills. But when will she learn that not everyone appreciates her meddling?

title: Empire of the Vampire
author: Jay Kristoff
description: With the sun vanished and vampires ascendant, Gabriel de León is humanity's last silversaint and their last hope. Imprisoned by his enemies, he recounts battles, heartbreak, and the perilous chase for the Holy Grail.

title: Fantastic Mr Fox
author: Roald Dahl
description: A clever fox and his family set out to outsmart their farming neighbours in this charmingly illustrated classic children's novel.

title: Far from the Madding Crowd
author: Thomas Hardy
description: Bathsheba Everdene thinks she's all that. Three men are reluctant to contradict her and eager to win her affections. A foggy, moody novel in a provincial setting with tragic plot twists and beautiful nature writing.

title: Feminist, Queer, Crip
author: Alison Kafer
description: In this work, Professor Alison Kafer proposes a critical framework that imagines another future for disabled and queer bodies and rejects the idea of disability as a predetermined limit.

title: Femme in Public
author: Alok V Menom
description: Queer artist Alok shares their journey navigating family and American society as a gender non-conforming, Indian diasporic, transfemme in this heartfelt collection of poems.

title: Ficciones
author: J. L. Borges, A. Bonner & A. Kerrigan
description: 17 masterful short stories from the Argentinian writer and poet, famous for his maze-like prose. Fantastical, intellectual, and bizarre. This selection includes The Library of Babel , The Circular Ruins , and The God of the Labyrinth .

title: The Field Guide; The Spiderwick Chronicles #1
author: Holly Black & Tony DiTerlizzi
description: When Jared, Simon, and Mallory dust off a field guide to the hidden world of faerie, the siblings learn the dangerous, fantastical creatures are a little too close to their new home. Book one of a magical children's series.

title: Five Little Peppers and How They Grew; Five Little Peppers #1
author: Margaret Sidney Porter
description: A cosy classic about five children and their mother, living in a little brown house, learning to be helpful and create their own happiness in lean times. Who knew baked goods and surprise visits could bring so much joy?

title: Five on a Treasure Island
author: Enid Blyton
description: A childhood adventure with five friends, a shipwreck, and a hidden treasure. The first in the classic Famous Five series of children's mystery novels.

title: Five Survive
author: Holly Jackson
description: Red and her five friends are headed for Spring Break at the beach. But when their RV breaks down, the young adults are stranded. A killer plans to silence one of their group. Can they find out who they want before the night takes them all?

title: A Florence Diary
author: Diana Athill
description: A charming diary, chronicling Athill's fortnight in Italy, 1947. Illustrated with delightful black and white photos of Florence, this little book captures an era of travel that has been lost to time.

title: Flower Fables
author: Louisa May Alcott
description: A collection of fairy stories and poems, Flower Fables is a charming and delightful book, illustrated and easy to read for children and adults of any age.

title: Flowers for Algernon
author: Daniel Keyes
description: A science-fiction short story turned novel, which grapples with the meaning of intelligence, disability, and the consequences of human augmentation in the name of progress.

title: The Forests of Silence; (Deltora Quest #1)
author: Emily Rodda
description: In this epic quest for young readers, a pair of unexpected heroes must face untold dangers as they search for the long magical gems that could save them from the tyrannical Shadow Lowd. Their first destination? The Forests of Silence.

title: The Forgotten Beasts of Eld
author: Patricia A. McKillip
description: Sybel's closest friends are magical animals. She's more than content to avoid the war brewing in neighboring kingdoms. But when a soldier brings a human baby into her fantastical menagerie for safekeeping, her safe little world will never be the same.

title: Frog and Toad Together
author: Arnold Lobel
description: Oh, to garden, bike, and go on adventures with your soulmate! While these short stories might strictly qualify as children's literature, who doesn't yearn for the life of Frog and Toad?

title: Full Dark, No Stars
author: Stephen King
description: Four chilling and devastating novellas by Stephen King, dealing with the darkness of retribution and revenge. True horror, read with care!

title: Games, Game Design, Game Studies
author: Gundolf S. Freyermuth
description: The must-read primer for anyone seeking to become a serious games scholar.

title: The Garden of Evening Mists
author: Tan Twan Eng
description: Set in post-war Malaya, this story follows Yun Ling, a war-crime survivor and retired judge, through a shifting timeline between 1980s and flashbacks to 1949, as she seeks solace in the lush highlands of her childhood.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
description: Following the blossoming relationship of Nick and Amy, we flash forward to their fifth wedding anniversary, where Amy has suddenly disappeared... Has Nick become a man capable of killing his wife?

title: Good Girl, Bad Blood
author: Holly Jackson
description: Student investigator turned podcaster Pippa is trying to leave her detective days behind. But how can she ignore this recent disappearance, when the police won't even investigate?

title: Good Night, Gorilla
author: Peggy Rathmann
description: When the zookeeper isn't looking, this little gorilla isn't the only animal who sneaks out of the zoo. A short and sweet bedtime story for the little ones.

title: A Gothic Cookbook; Hauntingly Delicious Recipes Inspired by 13 Classic Tales
author: Ella Buchan & Dr Allesandra Pino
description: Feast your way through thirteen Gothic stories, from The Bloody Chamber to The Woman in White. The illustrated cookbook that invites readers to devour the literary classics.

title: Gregor the Overlander
author: Suzanne Collins
description: Gregor discovers a hidden world beneath New York City in this charming, yet dangerous fantasy adventure for young readers. Will he live up to the prophecy foretelling his deeds?

title: Gulliver's Travels
author: Jonathan Swift
description: Through the various travels of Gulliver, this proto-science fiction novel satirises the political environment of England and the travelogues popular during its colonial expansions.

title: Hamlet
author: William Shakespeare
description: This Danish prince suddenly has a lot going on. His father is dead, his uncle is evil, and his mother is quickly getting remarried... So, it is entirely understandable that Hamlet now plunges into a crisis.

title: Hamnet
author: Maggie O'Farrell
description: Stratford-upon-Avon, 1596 - A marriage is on the rocks, and a sudden illness threatens the life of a child. A short, tragic, and intricate novel about the familial inspiration behind one of the world's most famous plays. It never mentions the playwright by name!

title: Heartstopper; Volume 1
author: Alice Oseman
description: The heartwarming graphic novel where Nick and Charlie meet at a grammar school for boys. Prepare to giggle and blush while watching sparks unfold between them!

title: Heidi
author: Johanna Spyri
description: The heartwarming story of little Heidi, who lives with her grandfather in the Swiss Alps, changing the lives of those around her for the better. A classic for children all around the world.

title: The Hobbit; The Lord of the Rings #0
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: You never know what'll happen when you step outside your front door. Especially if a wizard left his mark on said door. Bilbo leaves his creature comforts behind to seek adventure with a company of dwarves, and winds up bringing home the worst souvenir possible.

title: Homage to Catalonia
author: George Orwell
description: An exceptionally observant, vivid, and often witty journalistic work turned memoir by George Orwell, wherein he tells of his time fighting fascists in the Spanish Civil War.

title: Home Before Dark
author: Riley Sager
description: Her father's last words were: "Stay away from the house, it's not safe for you." Maggie gives her word. But later, she discovers she's inherited the spooky house that made her father famous. Can't hurt to visit... right? A horror/thriller with a book-within-a-book format.

title: Howl's Moving Castle
author: Diana Wynne Jones
description: Sophie seeks out the mysterious wizard Howl, and his ever-moving castle, since he might be her only chance of breaking her enchantment. Is there more to his heartlessness than meets the eye?

title: If Not, Winter; (Fragments of Sappho)
author: Sappho, transl. by A. Carson
description: A collection of ancient fragments, this book offers a glimpse into the captivating poetry of a mysterious Greek writer whose verses of passion (for women) have stood the test of time.

title: If We Were Villains
author: M. L. Rio
description: Seven acting students at an elite arts college are very familiar with Shakespearean drama. But soon, the fictional power struggles and love entanglements they enact become their reality, too.

title: The Illustrated Dust Jacket, 1920-1970
author: Martin Salisbury
description: In this collection of cover art, you'll see the historical evolution of style and intention in book jacket design: From practical tool to key marketing element. Go ahead and judge books by their cover!

title: In Cold Blood
author: Truman Capote
description: Murder, mystery, and chilling psychology intertwine in this pioneering work in the true crime genre, as Capote (and his friend Harper Lee) extensively research a 1959 case.

title: Inferno
author: Dante Alighieri, transl. by A. Esolen
description: The first part of the epic Divine Comedy , and the most famous work of self-insert bible fanfiction to date. Wherein Dante and Virgil delve deep through the nine circles of hell.

title: The Inheritance Games
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description: This thrilling mystery for young adults kicks off a series of novels surrounding Avery, a teenager who suddenly becomes heir to a strange billionaire's fortune. If she can make it that far...

title: It
author: Stephen King
description: This one will certainly make you afraid of clowns, balloons and storm drains... if you aren't already. A staple of small-town horror fiction, It makes children's nightmares a reality.

title: Italian Villas and Their Gardens
author: Edith Wharton
description: Sixteen years before her famous novel, The Age of Innocence , Wharton publishes this scholarly travel book. It is a remarkably detailed survey of Italian garden architecture.

title: James and the Giant Peach
author: Roald Dahl
description: This fantastical adventure follows James into a peachy realm populated by friendly worms and bugs. An illustrated book perfect for children.

title: Journey to the Centre of the Earth
author: Jules Verne
description: Have you always wanted to meet a dinosaur? Easy, just hop down an Icelandic volcano and check at the Earth's core. They should hopefully still be there.

title: Julie Chan is Dead
author: Liann Zhang
description: When Julie finds her influencer twin dead, she slips into her glamorous life. Designer wardrobe, perfect skin, millions of followers. But on an exclusice island retreat, she learns Chloe's world was far from flawless. And someone wants the new "Chloe" gone too.

title: Julius Caesar
author: William Shakespeare
description: Who's up for a political assassination with the homies? Come on. It's for the good of Rome, right? — No! Wrong! Et tu, Brute?!

title: Jurassic Park
author: Michael Crichton
description: IT'S JURASSIC PARK, IT'S A MASSIVE PARK! Filled with more dinosaurs and danger than you can shake a stick at. A slightly misguided scientist decided to give dinosaurs another chance, and thinks it would be great if the public could come and have a nose at them too.

title: Kiki's Delivery Service
author: Eiko Kadono
description: A spirited young witch needs to learn how to stand on her own two feet as she arrives in a bustling and charming seaside town. Sound familiar, anyone?

title: King Stakh's Wild Hunt
author: Uladzimir Karatkievich
description: Something stalks the foggy marsh as a young folklorist finds himself lost in a family's cursed manor. Will he be able to figure out or fall to the Wild Hunt ? Mysterious and gothic, this Belarusian classic continues to haunt.

title: Henry V
author: William Shakespeare
description: Shakespeare's next Henry must prove his might in a war against France in this dramatic retelling of English history. And he's certainly nailing the speeches!

title: Labyrinths
author: Jorge Luis Borges
description: Labyrinths: Selected Stories & Other Writings is a representative selection of essays, short stories, and parables written by Argentine poet Borges and translated into English.

title: Lady Audley's Secret
author: Mary Elizabeth Braddon
description: A scandalous domestic thriller complete with a twisty murder mystery, and a layered anti-heroine. Surprisingly feminist for the Victorian era!

title: Le Corbusier
author: Le Corbusier
description: Known as a designer of brutalist buildings, this collection of his projects illustrates Le Corbusier's belief in better living conditions for the increasingly crowded cities of the 20th century.

title: Leave Taking
author: Winsome Pinnock
description: A humorous play about a British-Caribbean mother and her two daughters transposing their Jamaican heritage in 1980's London. Leave Taking was the first play by a black female playwright to premiere at the Royal National Theatre in 1987.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
description: The four March sisters navigate love, loss, and the trials of growing up into womanhood, as their coming-of-age story reflects parts of Alcott's own youth.

title: Love
author: Toni Morrison
description: A contemporary classic by Morrison, which follows three generations of Black women, the aftermath of a man's death, and their complicated relationships to him and each other.

title: Macbeth
author: William Shakespeare
description: One couple of Scottish aristocrats start to believe that they deserve a bigger piece of the cake. And they decide to make it everyone else's problem...

title: Mend! A Refashioning Manual and Manifesto
author: Kate Sekules
description: Decrease the number of clothes you toss, and learn how to repair them in ways that make them a work of art! A how-to guide explaining the process and possibilities of mending, perfect for the experienced sewist or the person who's never picked up a needle.

title: Meridian
author: Alice Walker
description: The captivating story of Meridian Hill, a female activist in the Civil Rights Movement of the 1960s and 70s, and her political and personal revolutions in life.

title: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood
author: Howard Pyle
description: Follow the adventures of the merry bandit who robbed from the rich to give to the poor. Pyle, an American illustrator, wrote this version of the legend especially for children, and this edition features his humorous illustrations.

title: Merry Mister Meddle; Mister Meddle Series
author: Enid Blyton
description: A collection of humorous tales about Mister Meddle and his disastrous attempts at being helpful; like putting a 'growing-spell; in a wash-tub to help with laundry or mistaking glue for treacle that he uses to spruce up his aunt's pudding!

title: Middlemarch
author: George Eliot
description: A charming study of English provincial life, with all of its love, ambition, and scandal. Follow the lives of unforgettable characters in this literary classic.

title: milk and honey
author: Rupi Kaur
description: A poetic journey through heartbreak and healing and the hurt and love that come with 21st-century womanhood.

title: Misery
author: Stephen King
description: An obsessive fan has no plans of ever letting her favourite romance author go... Another cocaine-fueled 80s horror classic.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
description: A maniacal pursuit, an enigmatic white giant, and a captain obsessed with vengeance. A commercial failure, and "the greatest book of the sea ever written", according to Walter.

title: Momo; or, The Grey Gentlemen
author: Michael Ende
description: A strange story of time thieves and a curious child on a mission to return stolen time and joy to her town. Get inspired by this children's classic!

title: Journey to the West; or, Monkey King
author: Wu Cheng'en
description: A mischievous shapeshifter embarks on a legendary adventure, based on folk tales and legends, in this timeless Chinese classic.

title: The Journey; Big Panda and Tiny Dragon #2
author: James Norbury
description: The adventures of Big Panda and Tiny Dragon continue as they navigate some of life's trying moments. Accompanied by charming illustrations, this is a beautiful picture book about friendship and overcoming adversity.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
description: What better place to murder someone than on the world-famous Orient Express? Only the killer forgot that the genius detective Hercule Poirot is also on board.

title: Night Shift
author: Stephen King
description: No, not the Lucy Dacus song! It's a collection of spooky Stephen King short stories instead. Perfect for enthusiasts of 80s horror.

title: The Nightingale
author: Hans Christian Andersen
description: An emperor falls for a nightingale's song, but when a flashy mechanical bird appears, everyone forgets the real nightingale, and he flies away. A poetic tale that reminds us that no technology can truly capture the beauty of nature or one's talent.

title: Nimona
author: N. D. Stevenson
description: Shapeshifter Nimona's plan was to become the sidekick to newly-termed villain Ballister. But when the heroes are not as goodhearted as everyone believed, that plan might have to change last-minute...

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
description: A classic of dystopian social science fiction, for good reason. Totalitarianism, mass surveillance, and state oppression of nonconformity - 1984 has got them all.

title: Non-Binary Lives; An Anthology of Intersecting Identities
author: Various Authors
description: Exploring what it means to be non-binary in the 21st century, this collection of essays shares how the gender identities of non-binary people across diverse backgrounds intersect and impact other aspects of their lives.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
description: Follow Connell and Marianne as they grow up in Ireland, fall in love, struggle at school, and navigate their socioeconomic differences in this young romance novel.

title: Northanger Abbey
author: Jane Austen
description: A young fangirl of Gothic novels has to learn that dark romance is not always so appealing in real life. A deliciously satirical Austen classic.

title: The Notebooks of Malte Laurids Brigge
author: Rainer Maria Rilke
description: A deeply insightful near auto-biography, this book is bound to satisfy your urge for poetic prose but increase your urge for self-reflection - in the aristocratic, slightly depressing and very serious way. If you want to see death on every corner, this one's for you.

title: Notes From A Small Island
author: Bill Bryson
description: After two decades in Britain, this American author isn't afraid to draw his conclusions about the small, weird, lovely island that had become his second home.

title: One Of Us Is Lying
author: Karen M. McManus
description: When the Breakfast Club turns into a crime scene before detention is over, you know you'll be in for a thrilling, twisted mystery drama.

title: One Piece; Volume 1
author: Eiichiro Oda
description: Sail the seas in this action-packed manga with Monkey D. Luffy and his crew, the Straw Hat Pirates! Follow Luffy as he goes on a journey to search for the treasure One Piece, and become King of the Pirates.

title: Paper Towns
author: John Green
description: Margo is a mystery in human form, and Quentin would love nothing more than to solve her. The young adult novel for those who are looking to love for the answer.

title: Paradise
author: Toni Morrison
description: Morrison herself wanted to call this book War . Her groundbreaking novel chronicles the catastrophic happenings taking place in an all-Black Oklahoma town and its counterpart, the Convent.

title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
description: The 27-year-old Anne Elliot gets a second chance at love when her ex-fiance, Captain Frederick Wentworth, moves into her family's home. Another Austen classic that never gets old.

title: Pet Sematary
author: Stephen King
description: Sometimes, dead is better... Because whatever came back from the grave no longer answers to "Heeere, kitty!". Another horror staple from Maine's biggest fan, Stephen King.

title: Rambles in Germany and Italy; in 1840, 1842, and 1843
author: Mary Shelley
description: While Italy held many painful memories for Mary Shelley, she returned to the places she had once called home as a political ally in Italy's fight for independence.

title: Red Dragon
author: Thomas Harris
description: The first novel in the Hannibal Lecter series introduces us to the infamous psychologist and cannibal, as he finds an unlikely ally in FBI profiler Will Graham. Absolutely gruesome and disturbing!

title: The Red Virgin; Memoirs of Louise Michel
author: Louise Michel
description: In her memoirs, Louise Michel recounts her life as a revolutionary activist and educator, from the Paris Commune to her exile in New Caledonia. A true heroine of her time, the "Red Widow" affirms her anarchist, feminist, and anti-colonialist commitments.

title: Red, White & Royal Blue
author: Casey McQuiston
description: The charming, cheeky, and slightly steamy rom-com where a First Son of America falls in love with a British crown prince, causing chaos, scandal, and plenty of swooning moments.

title: Redwall; Book 1
author: Brian Jacques
description: Welcome to Redwall - An abbey that offers the sanctuary of good food, warm fires, and brave tales. This world is not without its dangers, but if a humble mouse can claim a fabled sword, they might just go down in song and legend!

title: Richard Serra; Interviews, etc., 1970-1980
author: Richard Serra
description: The Man Behind the Masterpieces: Explore the life and artistic vision of the legendary sculptor and modern art icon in this series of interviews, presented alongside marvellous black-and-white photographs of his life's work.

title: Romancero Gitano
author: Federico García Lorca
description: Eighteen romances where love and desire intertwine with violence and death. Lorca portrays the pride, resistance and suffering of the Romani people, their legends and traditions, revealing the hidden soul of Andalusia through rich symbolic poetry.

title: Romeo and Juliet
author: William Shakespeare
description: No matter how many times you've seen it before, you will always be swept away by the passion and despair of these two lovers. And you might even be surprised by your own emotions.

title: Salomé
author: Oscar Wilde
description: According to a reviewer of the play at its original performance, it is "an arrangement in blood and ferocity, morbid, bizarre, repulsive." Now, we might view Salomé as a symbol of modernity, a challenge and a revolt against a patriarchal Victorian society.

title: Saving Danny
author: Cathy Glass
description: One of Cathy Glass's many fostering memoirs, this is the story of Danny, who comes into her care when his parents can no longer cope with his learning difficulties. It's a powerful testament to how a little love and patience can change a child's life.

title: The Saviour Fish; Life and Death on Africa's Greatest Lake
author: Mark Weston
description: A captivating blend of travel writing and environmental reportage, this erudite work chronicles the author's life on remote Ukerewe Island in Lake Victoria, offering a profound perspective on ecological and cultural upheaval.

title: Second Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
description: Asimov's world-famous sci-fi epic continues as secrets unravel around the 14-year-old Arkady, alliances form in a war for the galaxy, and the true power of the Second Foundation is revealed.

title: Shakespeare; The World as Stage
author: Bill Bryson
description: Unravel the enigmatic genius behind Shakespeare's words, as explained by Bill Bryson. A great and light-hearted introduction for every reader interested in the man behind the plays.

title: Shatter Me
author: Tahereh Mafi
description: The first in a series of young adult novels, set in a dystopian world where one girl's touch is lethal. Will she finally escape the grasp of the government? And will she find love in the meantime?

title: Shearwater; A Bird, an Ocean, and a Long Way Home
author: Roger Morgan-Grenville
description: Intertwining memoir, nature writing, and travelogue, this book chronicles the author's year-long adventure in pursuit of the longstanding object of his fascination: the impressive seabird known as the Manx Shearwater, or Puffinus puffinus !

title: Shirley
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: Shirley is a traditional Brontë romance with a titular intelligent and headstrong heiress. Yet, the novel also deals with themes of economic struggles after the introduction of "labour-saving machinery". Sound familiar, anyone?

title: Six of Crows
author: Leigh Bardugo
description: Six of Crows continues the dark YA fantasy series set in the "Grishaverse". Join the criminally talented Kaz Brekker as he gets together a crew of fellow teenage thieves to complete a dangerous task.

title: Sky Island
author: L. Frank Baum
description: From Baum's much lesser known series of children's fantasy, Sky Island takes Trot, Button Bright, and Captain Bill to — you guessed it — an island in the sky. Illustrated by John R. Neill

title: Skyward; (Book 1)
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: Humanity is trapped on a planet under attack by mysterious aliens. Spensa, living among them, dreams of joining the pilots defending humanity. Join her, as she fights for a place in flight school and faces the harsh reality of war.

title: Slaughterhouse-Five
author: Kurt Vonnegut
description: Billy Pilgrim travels back and forth in time due to his post-war psychological trauma. Vonnegut combines his own experiences as an American soldier in 1945 Dresden with science-fictional elements to create one of the most revered anti-war novels of all time.

title: Small Spaces; (Book 1)
author: Katherine Arden
description: With little more than ominous advice and stories of "the smiling man," Ollie and her classmates find themselves in a chilling race for survival when their bus breaks down on the way home from a field trip in this spooky series starter.

title: Snow Crash
author: Neal Stephenson
description: Hiro Protagonist (yes, that's really his name) is a hacker and pizza delivery driver in a dystopian, futuristic America. who comes across a very dangerous data file in the Metaverse.

title: Stories of Your Life and Others
author: Ted Chiang
description: A collection of eight marvellous science-fiction short stories, asking the question that speculative fiction always asks best: "what if?"

title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
author: John Green
description: Turned from a podcast into John Green's first non-fiction book, the writer rates various phenomena of the age of human intervention in nature on a scale of 1 to 5 stars.

title: Antigone
author: Sophocles
description: The tale of a sister who will fight to honour her brothers after their death, no matter the cost. A tragic play about the strength of familial love and the consequences of defiance.

title: Antony and Cleopatra
author: William Shakespeare
description: A tragic play set during the founding of the Roman Empire in 30 BC. Bask in the hot mess of a relationship between Egyptian Queen Cleopatra and Roman General Mark Antony.

title: Anxious People
author: Fredrik Backman
description: An apartment showing becomes a hostage situation when a bank robber walks in. The catch: no one knows their identity! As the pressure builds, a collection of perfect strangers confess their deepest fears in this tender, mysterious, and furry story.

title: The Autograph Man
author: Zadie Smith
description: Alex-Li Tandem is a mess. He makes his living by selling celebrity autographs, drinks too much, cheats on his girlfriend, and is hunting down an American actress whose last film came out in the 1940s.

title: The Bad Beginning; (A Series of Unfortunate Events)
author: Lemony Snicket
description: When three siblings are suddenly orphaned, they have to live with their strange relative, Count Olaf. The failed actor wants to secure the family fortune for himself, but Violet, Klaus, and Sunny might stop him yet.

title: Bait and Witch; (Witch Way Librarian Mysteries #1)
author: Angela M. Sanders
description: Josie expected to lie low in Wilfred, Oregon for a bit when she took a job as the small town's only librarian. She didn't expect latent magic powers, a fight to save the library from being torn down, or finding a body in the woods, but has to tackle all three head-on.

title: Baking with Kim-Joy; Cute and Creative Bakes to Make You Smile
author: Kim-Joy
description: 40 recipes from the sunshine-filled Great British Bake Off finalist. If your desserts don't make your friends squeal with delight, are they even treats? This cookbook includes colourful instructions for making llama cookies, panda-madeleines, and choux bun turtles.

title: The Ballad of Jacquotte Delahaye
author: Briony Cameron
description: Get ready for a pirate adventure following Jacquotte's rise to the captaincy. Join her, her friends, and the woman she falls in love with in this epic tale of overcoming hardships and empowerment

title: The Bar Code Tattoo; (Bar Code #1)
author: Suzane Weyn
description: Everyone’s getting the bar code tattoo. When Kayla decides not to, her life as she knows it is thrown upside down and she finds herself on the run and wondering what exactly is the bar code tattoo – and why does everyone need one – in this YA sci-fi dystopia.

title: Barmy British Empire; Horrible Histories
author: Terry Deary
description: History of the British Empire is full of horrible people and horrible deeds. Find out how a war started when a Brit was sitting on a stool and who wore a necklace made of human skulls in this not-so-horribly-boring history book!

title: Baroque
author: John Rupert Martin
description: Aptly titled, Baroque covers the Baroque period of art and antiquity in Europe. There are 226 illustrations to go along with the drier descriptions, but if you read carefully, you'll become an amateur expert on the Baroque! How's that for a party trick?

title: The Battle of the Labyrinth
author: Rick Riordan
description: Percy Jackson and his friends must enter the Minoan labyrinth to continue their godly quest and fulfil another prophecy in this fourth entry in the Olympian fantasy series.

title: Battle Royale
author: Koushun Takami
description: Teens trapped on an island in a fight to the death? No, not that one! Junior high school students are forced to kill each other by a fictional, fascist Japanese government. The original novel has a powerful political message.

title: Beartown; Book 1
author: Fredrik Backman
description: Beartown's last ember of hope lies in the success of its youth hockey league. When a scandal breaks involving the star player and the manager's daighter, each town member must choose whether they're on the side of justice, or the dream of a chance at finally winning.

title: The Bell Jar
author: Sylvia Plath
description: Esther feels trapped in the confines of womanhood. After struggling with the expectations of marriage, sex, and work, and following multiple suicide attempts, she is hospitalised.

title: The Big Sleep
author: Raymond Chandler
description: The most heteronormatively masculine, "hard-boiled", noir detective story you'll ever read. In which PI Philip Marlowe uncovers a criminal plot and seduces "damsels" left and right.

title: The Binding
author: Bridget Collins
description: After a breakdown, young Emmett Farmer is apprenticed to a mysterious bookbinder. He learns to craft beautiful volumes that cage people's darkest secrets, yet one locked vault remains off-limits.

title: Binti; (Book 1)
author: Nnedi Okorafor
description: Binti is the first of the Himba to attend the intergalactic Oomza University. On her way she confronts prejudice, war, and an forges a world-changing connection. A shining example of Africanfuturism

title: Bird by Bird; Some Instructions on Writing and Life
author: Anne Lamott
description: The most difficult part of writing is just getting started! Author Anne Lamott gently guides the aspirational writer through each step of the writing journey. Learn how to observe, reflect, and give yourself plenty of grace through the process!

title: Birdland
author: Simon Stephens
description: Watch the unravelling of Paul, a rock star at the prime of his career, in this cautionary play about fame and celebrity culture.

title: Bleak House
author: Charles Dickens
description: A layered story about injustice and generosity, set amid the chaotic legal system of 19th-century London. The fortunes of many lie in the outcome of a twelve-year legal dispute. While lawyers quibble, drama, mystery, and tragedy unfold in the characters' daily lives.

title: The Blind Assassin
author: Margaret Atwood
description: Stories within stories intertwine in this gripping tale as Iris Chase looks back on decades of her life. She recalls her childhood, her sister, her failed marriage, a world war... and reveals many secrets along the way.

title: Blithe Spirit
author: Noel Coward
description: When a seance goes hilariously wrong, novelist Charles finds himself haunted by the ghost of his first wife, Elvira. Jealous of his new wife, Elvira acts out in desperation to keep Charles with her. A slapstick onstage farce of ghostly proportions!

title: The Bluest Eye
author: Toni Morrison
description: This Morrison novel does not shy away from dealing with the devastating and harrowing consequences of the violence and abuse that were (and are still) inflicted upon young Black girls.

title: Blurb Your Enthusiasm: A Cracking Compendium of Book Blurbs, Writing Tips, Literary Folklore and Publishing Secrets
author: Louise Willder
description: You pick up a book. What next? Maybe you read the hook on the back cover, the flaps, and the glowing blurbs authors give one another 'Astonishing!'... Did they even read it? Learn the humour and history behind the text outside of books! As meta as it gets.

title: Body in the Library; Miss Marple  #2
author: Agatha Christie
description: The body of a young woman is found in the library at the Bantry estate. Before the police question the neighbours, Mrs Bantry suggests they consult Miss Marple, a silver-haired woman with a keen ear for village gossip and a keen eye for human nature.

title: Book of Azrael
author: Amber V Nicole
description: He was a God; she was a demon—can I make it any more obvious? A true enemies to lovers and all the way back again, with her being the morally grey naughty one for a change.

title: The Canterville Ghost
author: Oscar Wilde
description: Wilde's first published story is a classic ghost tale with lots of humour. Because what could be more fun than a bold American family moving into an estate haunted by an English aristocrat?

title: Caps for Sale; A Tale of a Peddler, Some Monkeys and Their Monkey Business
author: Esphyr Slobodkina
description: A classic picture book about the dangers of taking naps under trees filled with monkeys. Hilarious and repetitive, what every child wants.

title: The Cask of Amontillado
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: Edgar did it again, a short story whose gruesome nature will linger much longer on your mind.

title: The Color Purple
author: Alice Walker
description: A striking epistolary novel that continuously insists on the solidarity, friendship, and romantic love between women of colour, even in the face of the greatest adversities.

title: The Colour of Magic; Discworld #1, Rincewind #1
author: Terry Pratchett
description: Wow! Is this that famous inn where all barbarians and adventurers get drunk and fight? As a wizard, Rincewind studied forms of intelligence that can be found in many alternate realities. Yet this tourist in Ankh-Morpork is a curious case in terms of intelligence.

title: The Comedy of Errors
author: William Shakespeare
description: This play might be less deep than what we are used to from Billy S., but the slapstick, puns, mishaps, and chaos could make any modern audience laugh.

title: The Comfort Book
author: Matt Haig
description: Matt saved all the little pieces of encouragement that kept him going, and put them in this book. This self-help book is an invitation to reflect and rebuild your hope. Take what you need!

title: The Complete Father Brown
author: G.K. Chesterton
description: Father Brown is an English crime-solving priest with a sympathetic ear and sharp insight into human nature. This collection comprises 49 cases featuring the beloved cassock-wearing, bicycle-riding detective in the fictional village of Kembleford.

title: The Complete Illustrated Encyclopedia of Birds of the World; A Detailed Visual Reference Guide To 1600 Birds And Their Habitats, Shown In More Than 1800 Pictures
author: David Alderton
description: Discover your environment one chirp, tweet or whistle at a time with this extremely detailed and very specific encyclopaedia. Do you really need more information than the title?

title: The Complete Peanuts; 1993-1994
author: Charles M. Schultz
description: This collector's edition series compiles all 50 years of Peanuts comic strips published in newspapers from 1950 to 2000. Each volume contains two years of Charlie Brown and Snoopy's adventures to make you laugh and break your heart.

title: The Complete Robot
author: Isaac Asimov
description: Sixty-two years after the first published instance of the word 'robot', Asimov collects his science-fiction short stories about the industrious automatons in this series.

title: The Crucible
author: Arthur Miller
description: Did you dance with the devil last night? A critique of McCarthyism in the 1950s, this play uses the 1692 Salem witch trials to show how theocracy and personal vindictiveness are dangerous breeding grounds for hysteria-induced persecution.

title: The Cruel Prince
author: Holly Black
description: Jude is a mortal living in the fae realm and is constantly tormented by the High Court. Worst of all is the youngest prince. But can she stand up to him without being roped into the intrigue of the palace?

title: Crying in H Mart
author: Michelle Zauner
description: A heartfelt memoir from the artist behind Japanese Breakfast. Michelle writes about how grief sent her back to her Korean heritage for grounding and comfort, including the dishes she used to share with her mother.

title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
author: Mark Haddon
description: Christopher might be only 15, but he notices things that others don't. When his neighbour's dog is suddenly killed, he wants to know what happened. This novel is unique in its use of maps, pictures, and diagrams!

title: Cyrano de Bergerac
author: Edmond Rostand
description: A 19th century romcom—Cyrano, a skilled wordsmith, fears confessing his love to Roxane due to his large nose. Instead, he gets another man to woo Roxane in his place by giving her the love letters Cyrano writes. A tragicomedic play written entirely in poetic verse.

title: The Decoration of Houses
author: Edith Wharton
description: Edith Wharton only became a writer at 40, and besides her many novels, she also wrote books on design, travel, and culture. At 60, she was the first woman to win a Pulitzer for Fiction. It is never too late to begin.

title: The Dispossessed
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: Are YOU looking for feminist, anarchist sci-fi? I'm told Le Guin's Hainish Cycle is the place to start. While this book is technically the fifth book in the series, it is also the first in the chronology. Confusing, I know.

title: The Duke and I
author: Julia Quinn
description: London's high society loves Daphne. Yet none of the eligible gentlemen are courting her so far. Can the brooding Duke of Hastings, who has no interest in marriage or society, help her raise her reputation?

title: The Essential Rumi
author: Rumi, transl. by Barks & Moyne
description: The poetry and philosophy of the 13th-century Persian scholar known as Rumi have been among the most influential works in history.

title: Eugene Onegin
author: Alexander Pushkin
description: Tatyana loves Eugene. Eugene thinks she's boring. Later, he wishes he had acted differently. A suspenseful Russian novel in Verse with a large cast of characters and plenty of philosophy to chew on!

title: Europe Through the Back Door; A Travel Skills Handbook
author: Rick Steves
description: Catch yourself thinking, "I could live here," on nearly every trip? Make the most of your time in Europe by acting like you already do . Let TV-famous travel guide Rick Steves teach you how to connect with locals, avoid scams, and have a stress-free trip.

title: Eurydice
author: Sarah Ruhl
description: This play is a love story. Or is it? It's hard to tell, with all the forgetting. Try again: this is a maybe love story about Eurydice, who dies on her wedding day and is taken to the underworld. Orpheus is coming to rescue her, but Eurydice is starting to forget day by day.

title: Evelina
author: Frances Burney
description: Evelina is a naive young woman who learns first-hand about the dangers of fashionable society. A sharply comedic painting of excess, love, and women's status in eighteenth-century London. A novel from one of Jane Austen's favorite authors!

title: Eye of the Storm; (Reel Magic Series)
author: Meridwen Tidewell
description: After a wild storm haunts Bookstonbury's shores, four adventurous kids find a mischievous mermaid by an old shipwreck. Sneaking kelp tea and dodging nosy adults, they decode slippery clues to help her uncover something fishy hidden beneath the waves.

title: The Eyes of Darkness
author: Dean Koontz
description: A year after her son's death, Tina begins seeing things... Did Danny really die in an accident? And who is trying to conceal the truth from her? A paranormal horror-thriller.

title: The Fall of the House of Usher
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: American Gothic at its finest. Much like their protagonists, you will never be quite the same after diving into these deliciously dark stories.

title: Famous Last Words
author: Gillian McAllister
description: Camilla's husband disappears, leaving a cryptic note. By noon, he's the gunman in a London hostage siege. As police close in, she's the only one who understands the message he left and the only person who can stop what comes next.

title: The Fault in Our Stars
author: John Green
description: In the cancer support group her mother made her go to, 16-year-old Hazel meets Augustus. They share a love for books and metaphors and make each other rethink what it means to live, and what it means to die.

title: The Glass Castle
author: Jeannette Walls
description: Journalist Jeannette Walls recounts her unstable childhood and the fraught relationship with her parents in this bestselling memoir.

title: The God of Small Things
author: Arundhati Roy
description: The God of Small Things tells the dramatic story of twins from Kerala, India. They recall their childhood in 1969, as they grew up surrounded by family misery, political unrest, and forbidden love.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: The glamorous tale of love and wealth that shaped the cultural imagination of "the roaring 1920s". Yet this story doesn't shy away from confronting the unknown dark sides of the "American Dream".

title: The Handmaid's Tale
author: Margaret Atwood
description: A dystopian tale that imagines a totalitarian state in which the majority of women have been stripped of their freedom and reproductive rights to serve a Christian fundamentalist elite of men and their wives.

title: The Happy Prince and Other Tales
author: Oscar Wilde
description: A charming collection of illustrated children's tales written by the famous Irish playwright. Also includes The Nightingale and the Rose , The Selfish Giant , The Devoted Friend , and The Remarkable Rocket .

title: Hard Times
author: Charles Dickens
description: Meet Bouderby and Gradgrind, two men of industry. Their flawed views on life are evident in the outlooks of three children: Louisa, Thomas, and Cecilia. A comedic romance set amid the smoggy circus of mid-19th-century industrial society.

title: Hatchet
author: Gary Paulsen
description: A 13-year-old boy named Brian gets stranded in the Canadian wilderness and has to survive with nothing but the damaged supplies from the plane wreck. Alone, but with the luck of the young, Brian takes on the great outdoors and learns he's not half bad at hunting.

title: The Hidden Staircase; (Nancy Drew #2)
author: Carolyn Keene
description: Join the clever teenage detective Nancy Drew as she solves the mystery of a mysterious haunting. A detective story for all ages.

title: The Hunger Games
author: Suzanne Collins
description: The twelve districts of Panem are barely held under control. To keep them from revolting, children from each are chosen for gladiator-like games. There can only be one survivor, so Katniss can't let her little sister be picked.

title: The Importance of Being Earnest
author: Oscar Wilde
description: A hilarious and clever tale and a must-read for any fans of the Irish writer. A play that satirises Victorian society, from the author who ruffled many societal feathers.

title: The Invasion; (Animorphs #1)
author: K. A. Applegate
description: Only 90s kids will remember wanting the ability to spontaneously transform into an animal. But be careful, because aliens are trying to infiltrate Earth and, if you don't change back, you might get stuck as a hawk forever!

title: The Invention of Hugo Cabret
author: Brian Selznick
description: A mysterious tale about a young boy living in a Paris train station. With sparse pages of text, the story is told mostly through black-and-white illustrations, theatrically revealing tiny details of each scene-and Hugo's secret invention- one frame at a time .

title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
author: V.E. Schwab
description: Addie Larue once made a deal with the devil. Now she wanders the world as a ghost, forgotten by everyone she meets. Follow Addie's journey to find meaning to her existence as she learns to leave her mark on the world, and discovers a man who can remember her name.

title: The Invisible Man
author: H. G. Wells
description: A mysterious stranger appears at a village inn, causing chaos with the experiments he hides in his room. When he is discovered to have made himself invisible, a wild chase ensues. A thrilling classic of early science fiction.

title: Is a River Alive
author: Robert MacFarlane
description: Robert MacFarlane travels from Ecuador's cloud-forests to India's wounded waterways and Canada's wild rivers, asking a radical question: What if rivers are alive? A luminous blend of travel, nature writing, and urgent environmental insight.

title: The Island of Missing Trees
author: Elif Shafak
description: A tale of forbidden love and common roots set on the divided island of Cyprus in 1974. This story is told through multiple perspectives, shifting time, place, and species. The main narrator is a fig tree!

title: The Last Battle; (Chronicles of Narnia)
author: C.S. Lewis
description: It is almost Judgment Day in Narnia. Like, actual Christian Judgment Day. Where Lion Jesus sends all of the good guys to heaven at the end. The metaphor is no longer subtle at all.

title: The Last Time I Lied
author: Riley Sager
description: Emma remembers the night her cabin mates snuck out... Some of it. The memory gaps still haunt her. Fifteen years later, she reluctantly returns to camp Nightingale, and it feels like someone's waiting for her to break. A chilling and twisty YA thriller!

title: The Last Wish; (The Witcher)
author: Andrzej Sapkowski
description: A dark and dangerous story about fate, sorcery, and monstrous creatures. Accompany the Witcher, Geralt of Rivia, on his reluctant adventure, where he discovers curses, promises, and lovers.

title: Life is Better When You Draw It
author: Koosje Koene
description: To draw what you see, you need to take in all the details of that moment, which makes you more aware of the moment you are living in and thus enjoy it more. This book is not here to teach you how to draw, but to inspire you to draw, nonprofessionally!

title: The Lighthouse Mystery; The Boxcar Children #8
author: Gertrude Chandler Warner
description: Henry, Jessie, Violet, and Benny's days in a boxcar are behind them. Now they travel the world, solving mysteries nobody wanted their help with! This summer, the sibling are asleep in a lighthouse when their dog Watch wakes them, barking at something unseen.

title: The Lightning Thief; (Percy Jackson #1)
author: Rick Riordan
description: In this tale of greek mythology, friendship and mediocre paternal figures for the ages, our young protagonist has to go on a mythic roadtrip to retrieve a stolen artifact or face Zeus's wrath.

title: Little Lord Fauntleroy
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
description: Cedric, a middle-class American boy, learns he's heir to an English earldom. In the 1880s, this book popularized a trend in boys' fashion and set a legal precedent when the author insisted on compensation for theatrical adaptations of her work! Show me the money!

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
description: An enchanting tale of love, loss and an adventurous little prince who explores the universe and his own feelings. One sees clearly only with the heart . A must read for all ages.

title: The Lorax
author: Dr. Seuss
description: A furry creature speaks for the trees and shows us how capitalism is destroying nature. Don't be fooled by the clever rhymes, this children's book is a razor-sharp critique and hard-hitting warning.

title: The Lost Symbol
author: Dan Brown
description: Once again, symbologist Robert Langdom has to decode the secrets of old to save his mentor. This time in Washington D.C., there are undiscovered mysteries waiting for him.

title: The Lost Words; A Spell Book
author: Robert Macfarlane & Jackie Morris
description: Gone are the days when children's alphabets began with A for Acorn , B for Butterfly and C for Caterpillar . But in this book of spellbinding poetry and enchanting illustrations, the magical words of nature, travel, and animals are restored into our lives.

title: The Love Hypothesis
author: Ali Hazelwood
description: To convince her friends that she is over her ex, PhD student Olive convinces her young professor Adam to start a fake relationship. An example of fanfiction turned published book at its best.

title: Lysistrata
author: Aristophanes
description: A delightfully devious play demonstrating the power of women and shared protest through unconventional means. Will the booty be too strong to resist for Lysistrata and her friends? Or will they bring an end to the Peloponnesian War?

title: Madeline
author: Ludwig Bemelmans
description: Follow the adventures of 7-year-old Madeline in this illustrated children's book set in picturesque Paris. Spirited and brave in signature yellow, she navigates boarding school alongside her friends. A children's classic, loved throughout time, with memorable rhymes.

title: The Magic City
author: Edith Nesbit
description: Out of discontent with his new life, young Philip builds a city out of his toys, books, and game pieces. Next thing he knows, he appears in a life-size version of it, populated with people who need his and Lucy's help.

title: The Magic World
author: Edith Nesbit
description: This collection contains twelve beautiful and poetic short stories for children, including tales of talking animals, monarchs, fairies and beasts, and magical worlds.

title: The Maid; Molly the Maid #1
author: Nita Prose
description: The first book in a mystery series with a lovable, neurospicy protagonist at its heart. Molly loves her job cleaning rooms at Regency Grand Hotel, but her gullibility makes her both an unreliable narrator and the perfect suspect for a murder mystery!

title: The Martian Chronicles
author: Ray Bradbury
description: This classic sci-fi short-story cycle chronicles the exploration and settlement of Mars by the U.S. in the far and distant future of 2030. Bradbury explores militarism, genocide, oppression, and censorship from his post-war perspective.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: Astro-botanist Mark Watney is left behind on Mars after his crew narrowly escaped a dust storm. Alone and without supplies, the incorrigible optimist has to improvise in order to survive.

title: The Massacre of Mankind
author: Stephen Baxter
description: Following on from the events in the War of the Worlds, the world has relaxed, safe in the knowledge of how to defeat the Martian Menace. But how should they be? London is a totalitarian dystopia, and nobody is as prepared as they should be...

title: Maybe You Should Take to Someone; A Therapist, Her Therapist, and Our Lives Revealed
author: Lori Gottlieb
description: Lori Gottlieb is a therapist who needs therapy. As she tells the stories of her (nameless) patients, she recognizes themes in common with her own self-talk. A funny and hopeful memoir about our shared desires and capacity for change.

title: The Maze Runner
author: James Dashner
description: Thomas wakes up among other teenagers in the centre of an ever-changing maze without his memories. He soon learns that all they can do to survive is to try and escape by any means necessary.

title: The Murder at the Vicarage
author: Agatha Christie
