description: A quaint village, a nosy vicar and a most sinister murder. Join Miss Marple, the Queen of Crime, on a typical English murder mystery, full of exaggerated characters and dry wit.

title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd (Hercule Poirot Series)
author: Agatha Christie
description: This famous whodunnit harbours a twist you might not see coming. As detective Hercule Poirot leaves retirement to review the crime scene, all signs point to a locked room that no one could have gotten into.

title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
author: Agatha Christie
description: A book of many beginnings. The start of Christie's career as a prolific crime novelist. The first appearance of beloved Belgian detective Hercule Poirot. And a first in a long series of brilliant and suspenseful whodunnits.

title: The Mysterious Benedict Society; The Mysterious Benedict Society #1
author: Trenton Lee Stewart
description: Four children pass a series of curious tests to qualify for an undercover operation. Their mission: find out what's happening at the Learning Institute for the Very Enlightened. Contains buckets of friendship, weird inventions, and adventure!

title: The Namesake
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
description: Born in America to Indian parents, but named for a Russian author, it's no wonder that Gogol's life is marked by identity crisis. The moving novel The Namesake presents a portrait of Gogol and his immigrant family, exploring the challenges and relationships that come with evolving cultural values.

title: Nana; Volume 1
author: Ai Yazawa
description: When two young women with the same name become roommates, they also become allies in the pursuit of romance and punk rock dreams. This iconic manga series promises love, drama and a sense of fashion that can't be beat.

title: The Napoleon of Notting Hill
author: Gilbert K. Chesterton
description: In this alternate universe, successors of the Throne of England are chosen through random selection. And while the newest king fails to take his position seriously, one inhabitant of Notting Hill upholds his whimsical decisions with vigour.

title: Nation
author: Terry Pratchett
description: Mau is the only member of his nation since a huge wave destroyed his village and wiped out his tribe. Now all alone, this boy defies death and demands answers: Why did the gods let this happen to the elders? Who will judge whether he becomes a man or remains a boy?

title: Nature; Encyclopedia of Discovery
author: Various Authors
description: Discover the wonders of the natural world, from plants and animals to volcanoes and outer space. The immersive illustrations and diagrams make learning a delight for all ages.

title: The Neverending Story
author: Michael Ende
description: When a little boy hides in the attic with a strange book, an exciting adventure begins in the book's fantasy world. A story about escapism and imagination for all of us who enjoyed hiding in our books.

title: Nevermoor; The Trials of Morrigan Crow (Nevermoor #1)
author: Jessica Townsend
description: Cursed to die on her 11th birthday Morrigan is instead whisked away to a world she never knew existed to compete for membership in a secret society/ Sure, it's a preferable fate - but that doesn't mean it'll be easy!

title: The New Encyclopedia of British, European & African Birds
author: David Alderton
description: This illustrated guide is a perfect companion for birdwatching, a scientific encyclopedia to start learning about birds and a source of inspiration for a birdwatching trip in Europe or Africa!

title: New Hampshire
author: Robert Frost
description: A collection of poems and first Pulitzer Prize winning work by Robert Frost. His work is best known for its somber tone and descriptions of nature. Contains highly influential poems such as Fire and Ice and Nothing Gold Can Stay .

title: The Outsiders
author: S. E. Hinton
description: Written by the author when she was still a teenager herself, this coming-of-age novel is known for dealing with the socio-economic struggles of White American working-class teenagers and the "greaser" gangs they formed.

title: The Passage
author: Justin Cronin
description: The test subjects of a virus experiment develop strong physical and psychic abilities which cannot be controlled. The virus is spread and 90 years later, only a few colonies survive. One of them encounters the strange Amy...

title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
author: Stephen Chbosky
description: Charlie doesn't fit in anywhere at his new school. He grapples with grief and flashbacks to his aunt's death. But two seniors take him under their wing, and Charlie experiences all the joy and despair of growing up.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description: The Narcissus myth of the Victorian times, Wilde's novel is a wonderfully Gothic exploration of the values of beauty, sensuality, and hedonism in their opposition to morality and social norms.

title: A Place to Hang the Moon
author: Kate Albus
description: William, Edmund, and Anna need a guardian, so they slip into a crowd of evacuating London children, hoping to find a home. Nora, a friendly librarian, is the target of local gossip because of her German husband. But she has plenty of books, and makes a mean hot cocoa!

title: The Poems of Emily Dickinson; Volume II
author: Emily Dickinson
description: A comprehensive collection of poetry written by a woman who never received much recognition for her work while she was alive.

title: The Ramayana
author: Valmiki
description: This epic folk-tale was first composed around 300 BCE and was hugely influential on storytellers of later eras. Discover a modernised version and dive into heroics, battles with demons, and philosophical and spiritual wisdom.

title: The Raven
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: Once upon a dreary midnight, our protagonist is haunted by a raven, in this beautifully painfull poem about love and loss. Warning, it might leave you pondering weak and weary.

title: The Sea of Monsters; (Percy Jackson #2)
author: Rick Riordan
description: Mythical monsters, cursed cruise ships and unexpected friends accompany our Olympian teenagers in this divine sequel to the fantastic Percy Jackson series.

title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description: This historical drama follows Evelyn Hugo, an old Hollywood star, as she prepares her spicy tell-all biography, full of highs and lows, love and tragedies.

title: The Seven Lamps of Architecture
author: John Ruskin
description: This dry essay is a must-read for fans of gothic revival and a fun insight into the minds of 1800s mid-century architects. If you've ever wondered how architects 200 years ago contemplated their craft, this one's for you.

title: The Shining
author: Stephen King
description: A haunted hotel, a writer with writer's block, his fraught marriage, and the creepiest children in literature. What could possibly go wrong?

title: The Silence of the Lambs
author: Thomas Harris
description: A chilling thriller that won't let you go. Follow an FBI trainee as she struggles to cooperate with a cunning and cannibalistic psychopath to catch another serial killer.

title: The Silmarillion
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: Tolkien finally takes his time to write his own religious scripture about the creation of Middle-earth. Perfect for all closeted fantasy-theologians.

title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
author: Unknown & Simon Armitage
description: In this epic 14th-century poem, a green knight on a green horse (do they eat green eggs and ham?) arrives at Camelot on Yuletide. He throws his glove, an open challenge to King Arthur's knights. Sir Gawain accepts the wager, but he has no clue what he's in for!

title: Siren Queen
author: Nghi Vo
description: Magic weaves itself into every fibre of the Golden-Age, where survival isn't guaranteed, as magic binds those seeking fame to a future of blood, sweat, and sacrifices. In order to make it, Luli Wei may have to give up everything - including the women she loves - in this stunning historical fantasy.

title: The Song of Achilles
author: Madeline Miller
description: A marvellous retelling of the timeless classical epos, the Iliad, that focuses on the things that really matter. Complicated parents, the merciless politics of war, and, of course, the greatest love story of them all.

title: Sorcery and Small Magics; The Wildersongs Trilogy #1
author: Maiga Doocy
description: Leovander Loveage has a problem. His charms got mixed up, and now he's been cursed to obey any command by his academic rival, the sullen Sebastian Grimm. Now they have to find a counterspell, and fast, in this first book of this queer fantasy series!

title: Soul Music; Discworld #16, Death #3
author: Terry Pratchett
description: This novel could be about sex and drugs and rock 'n roll, but it is about a rock band. Also, there is a troll in the band, and a dwarf, and a suspiciously elvish-looking guy. The medieval ears of Discworld's citizens will hear metal, DEATH metal, so to speak!

title: The Soul of Man Under Socialism
author: Oscar Wilde
description: Wilde sharply outlines the economic realities of his time and prescribes humanistic socialism as a cure. What might have been a hot take today was instead published as an essay packed with stellar quotes in 1891.

title: The Spear Cuts Through Water
author: Simon Jimenez
description: You sit in a theatre, eyes riveted on the stage, as a brutal yet hopeful tale of gods, magic, and queer love unfolds in front of you. In this gripping novel, Jimenez turns the reader into an audience and forces them along on a pilgrimage to end a dynasty.

title: The Stand
author: Stephen King
description: A guttingly dark exploration of a bioweapon-turned-pandemic wiping out most of humanity, and the struggle of good vs. evil amongst the survivors left in its wake. Not for the faint of heart.

title: The Story Girl; Book 1
author: L.M. Montgomery
description: Fourteen-year-old Sara Stanley is a born storyteller. Both kids and grown-ups are captivated by her tales. Bev and his younger brother Felix spend a summer full of stories with their new friend Sara, hanging on every word.

title: The Tell-Tale Heart
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: Ba-bump, ba-bump, ba-bump. You killed someone and now the investigators are here. Ba-bump, ba-bump, ba-bump. Surely they must hear it, too. How will Poe's delightfully chilling short story end?

title: The Tempest
author: William Shakespeare
description: In this Shakespearean classic, a wizarding scholar is disposed of by his brother and forced to take a sabbatical on a desolate island. A play full of thundering monologues, magical confusions and romantic distractions.

title: The Templars; The Rise and Spectacular Fall of God's Holy Warriors
author: Dan Jones
description: A faltering war in the Middle East. A band of elite knights ready to die for Christianity's holiest sites. A secret financial empire answerable to no king and a deadly conspiracy built on lies...

title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
author: Anne Brontë
description: Gilbert is curious about Helen, the quiet woman who moved into Wildfell Hall with her young son. A gothic romance novel with femjnist themes. So ahead of its time that Anne's sister Charlotte hid it from publishers until after Anne's death.

title: The Traitor Baru Cormorant; (The Masquerade #1)
author: Seth Dickinson
description: After her home is colonised by Falcrest, Baru vows to climb the political ranks and destroy the empire from within to free her people. The first in a hard fantasy series filled with political intrigue and lesbian yearning, with a twist ending that will break your heart.

title: A Tramp Abroad
author: Mark Twain
description: An unserious, humorous, mix of real and fictional accounts of travel across Europe. Exaggerated events, his struggle with the German language, and other tales color his journey.

title: The Travels of Marco Polo
author: Marco Polo
description: In this totally real travelogue from the 13th century, we follow the author's self-insert — conveniently named Marco Polo — on his legendary travels from Venice to Beijing.

title: Wars of The Roses; The Fall of the Plantagenets and the Rise of the Tudors
author: Dan Jones
description: The Hollow Crown: 15th-century England-Five kings, endless war. Plantagenets rip themselves apart in the Wars of the Roses. Agincourt glory, Towton bloodbath, Richard III's murdered nephews...

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: A hefty chonk indeed. A famous historical novel with a meandering plot between - you guessed it: war and peace. As much about choosing the right life partner as it is about the Napoleonic Wars.

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H. G. Wells
description: One of the first instances of Martians invading Earth. How will humanity defend itself? A great example of the what if they did to us what we did to others kind of sci-fi horror.

title: The Well at the World's End
author: William Morris
description: Turns out the brilliant poet and designer William Morris also wrote a Fantasy classic. This beautifully illustrated book follows a young adventurer in an action-packed world of fading magic.

title: The Wilder Shores of Love
author: Lesley Blanch
description: An engaging account of four women from the nineteenth century who threw off their corsets and escaped their boring, conventional lives to find love and adventure on the wilder shores of the Middle East.

title: Will You Love Me?; The story of my adopted daughter Lucy
author: Cathy Glass
description: In this two-part fostering memoir, Cathy Glass shares the story of Lucy's journey, told from the perspectives of both her birth mother and foster mother, revealing how their lives became intertwined.

title: The Willows
author: Algernon Blackwood
description: This wonderfully twisted gothic horror classic follows two friends on a fateful canoe trip. Scary campsite encounters and weird nature—this otherworldly thriller will make you relieved to be in the comfort of your home.

title: The Woman in White
author: Wilkie Collins
description: The young art teacher Walter Hartright finds himself entangled in a complicated family mystery. Will he find out the underlying secret that led to the tragedy? Be prepared for a twist in this spooky classic.

title: Women Travel Solo; 30 Inspiring Stories of Adventure, Curiosity and the Power of Self-Discovery
author: Various Authors
description: Solo travel can be intimidating! This anthology will encourage you to book that trip. Read bout the experiences and personal revelations of 30 female solo travelers, complete with scenic photographs to encourage your wanderlust.

title: Women, Race and Class
author: Angela Y. Davis
description: In this groundbreaking essay, Angela Y. Davis explores the intersection of race, class, and gender, and how these factors shape the experiences of women in society. A foundational text in intersectional feminist theory.

title: Working Songs of Bookstonbury
author: Edwin Kimble
description: A collection of traditional shanties and sea songs by sailors and dockworkers around Bookstonbury harbour. Contains some old classics, as well as lesser-known local songs like The Net-Eating Shark and Even The Seagulls Like A Good Book .

title: The Yellow Fairy Book
author: L. B. Alleyne & A. Lang
description: A collection of some of the most well-known fairytales of European history. The many folktales, from Icelandic to Ukrainian to Estonian to Greek, are translated and edited for all children to enjoy.

title: Yellowface
author: R.F. Kuang
description: June steals Athena's novel and reinvents herself as a literary star, until the truth starts leaking through the cracks. A thrilling story of fame, fraud, and one very persistent ghost of a reputation.

title: Theodora Hendrix and the Curious Case of the Cursed Beetle
author: Jordan Kopy
description: Theodora lives with her spooky family, Mummy the mummy, Dracula, and the rest of the Monstrous League of Monsters. Join her as she fights to protect her family against the threat of the MLM Mansion!

title: There's A Ghost In This House
author: Oliver Jeffers
description: Tour a spooky little house with a friendly little ghost! This creatively printed children's book alternates from grayscale illustrations to transparent vellum pages, so the pale ghost appears to float through the pages.

title: They Both Die at the End
author: Adam Silvera
description: Life's expiration date is non-negotiable in this heart-wrenching story of two teenage boys spending their last 24 hours together. A story of love, hope, and death.

title: The Third Gilmore Girl; A Memoir
author: Kelly Bishop
description: From A Chorus Line to Gilmore Girls, Kelly Bishop has seen it all. Now she spills the stories: showbiz highs, Vegas lows, iconic roles, and the unforgettable people she met along the way. A lively, candid memoir from a legend.

title: This Book Will Bury Me
author: Ashley Winstead
description: After her father's death, Janeway finds a vehicle for her grief and unanswered questions: true crime discussion boards. She'll do anything to chase down new leads on a cold case, but her new online friends are hiding dark secrets of their own. An unputdownable thriller!

title: Titus Andronicus
author: William Shakespeare
description: Follow the worst of the Romans, as he does the worst things in the worst ways possible. An incredibly violent Shakespeare play, not for the faint of heart, filled with revenge, monologues, and pies.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: A timeless story of justice and innocence in a small Southern town where a lawyer takes on a charged case amid the prejudices and tensions of Depression-era Alabama.

title: To the Lighthouse
author: Virginia Woolf
description: The Ramsay family spends the summer on the Isle of Skye with a few of their guests. Among them, a young painter observes the tensions and relationships between the family members and how they change 10 years later.

title: A Tomb With a View; The Stories and Glories of Graveyards
author: Peter Ross
description: Uncovering the histories of those lying in a place where time stands still. Peter Ross pays homage to the famous, the infamous, and the forgotten in graveyards across Britain and Ireland. A book for all the taphophiles out there!

title: Treasure Island
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: A young boy finds himself in the possession of a pirate treasure map in this classic story of treachery and treasure that will have your kids dreaming of becoming a pirate.

title: Tree Houses: Baumhäuser - Maisons Dans les Arbres
author: Philip Jodidio
description: This trilingual book shows that building tree houses is not just fun for children. Beautiful pictures and descriptions of 30 tree houses from around the world: From private dream homes to luxury restaurants to a cathedral.

title: True Beauty; Volume 1
author: Yaongyi
description: After being bullied for her appearance in middle school, Jugyeong starts over with a new look. After mastering the art of makeup, none of her new friends know what her face really looks like. The first print of the popular Korean webtoon.

title: True Crime Story
author: Joseph Knox
description: In 2011, 19-year-old Zoe Nolan left a party at her flat and disappeared. Seven years later, writer Evelyn Mitchell is investigating the missing girl. Troubled by her findings, Evelyn consults Knox, a crime writer. A thriller so stacked with evidence, it feels real.

title: True Grit
author: Charles Portis
description: It's 1878, and fourteen-year-old Mattie wants vengeance . Tom Chaney took her father's life, his horse, and $150 in cash. Mattie convinces Rooster Cogburn, the toughest U.S. Marshal in the west, to accompany her in a manhunt across Indian territory.

title: The Truth; Discworld #25, Industrial Revolution #2
author: Terry Pratchett
description: Hear ye, hear ye! Ankh-Morpork has just invented the newspaper, the so-called source of the Truth. They thought revealing the Truth about political corruption and magical intrigues would blow citizens' minds, but a funny-shaped fruit is all the readers talk about!

title: Tuesdays with Morrie
author: Mitch Alborn
description: Over many meaningful conversations made during many Tuesday visits, the author reconnects with his dying college professor, Morrie. This short-but-moving memoir reflects on life's greatest questions.

title: The Turn of the Screw
author: Henry James
description: A young governess slowly realizes the two children under her care are the target of the creepy ghosts who haunt the estate. The troubling part is that Flora and Miles seem perfectly fine with it. Worst job ever.

title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
author: Jules Verne
description: In this steampunk classic, a group of scientists around Captain Nemo unexpectedly embarks on an unforgettable underwater adventure in the Nautilus .

title: Twisted Love
author: Ana Huang
description: In romance, there is something for everyone. This book is for the crowd who hear "possessive asshole, and her brother's best friend" and swoon.

title: The Unmaking of June Farrow
author: Adrienne Young
description: Eventually, each Farrow woman begins to see, hear, and smell things that aren't there, slowly unravelling their grip on reality. June is starting to see the signs. A mysterious novel about the doors we choose, and how those choices shape who we become and who we love.

title: Unmasking Autism
author: Devon Price
description: This book shares the author's personal experience with Autistic masking, extensive research on the history of the topic, as well as actionable advice and exercises to encourage self-expression. A ground-breaking work on neurodiversity.

title: The Unusual Suspects; The Sisters Grimm #2
author: Michael Buckley, Peter Ferguson (Illustrator)
description: Granny Relda tells Sabrina and Daphne the truth about their legacy. That classic book of fairytales? It's actually a casebook of magical crimes. Oh, and their new school in Ferryport Landing may have monsters. The second volume in the series of Fractured fairy tales.

title: Unwitting Wisdom; An Anthology of Aesop's Animal Fables
author: Helen Ward
description: A collection of twelve of Aesop's  fables, brought to life with beautiful illustrations. Discover the allegories that have enchanted children over 2500 years.

title: Upgrading and Repairing PCs
author: Scott Mueller
description: The definitive guide to everything PC-related. Scott really makes it sound easy—a book for PC repair enthusiasts and those who might want to upgrade all the way to an unbelievable 64 megabytes of RAM!

title: Valperga
author: Mary Shelley
description: A historical novel set in the Middle Ages, by certified goth nerd Mary Shelley. Mirroring the struggles of women in Shelley's time, the female protagonist must choose between love and political liberty.

title: Vera Wong's Unsolicited Advice for Murderers; Vera Wong #1
author: Jesse Q. Sutanto
description: A dead man in her tea shop? Vera Wong barely blinks. After all, who's better suited to solve a murder than a sixty year old tea connoisseur with weaponized mum-curiosity? The police don't stand a chance.

title: Villainous Victorians; Horrible Histories
author: Terry Deary
description: Teachers may tell you Victoria's Britain was an exciting place, but it was also a time for cruelty and wickedness. Read on for all the vile facts about the villainous Victorians, peppered with horribly hilarious humour that will keep you turning pages!

title: Villette
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: Lucy is hired as a governess in Villette, France, where she faces loneliness, illness, friendship, and eventually love. A novel famous for its plot twists, thanks to a narrator who frequently hides information from the readers.

title: Violets Are Blue
author: James Patterson
description: In this thrilling and bloody case, Detective Alex Cross investigates another macabre murder with undeniable signs of vampires while being haunted by someone from his past.

title: Watchmen; (Issue #12)
author: Alan Moore
description: In the world of Watchmen , superheroes emerged in the 1940s and altered history as we know it with their presence. Tune in for the twelfth and last issue of the iconic comic series.

title: Watership Down
author: Richard Adams
description: A journey of rabbits to find a new home, where they'll have to outwit enemies, "allies," and what seems to be every single one of the Prince's Thousand Enemies, for even when you reach the end, you find it's not that simple.

title: Where the Wild Things Are
author: Maurice Sendak
description: As a child, throwing a tantrum is fun and all, until you find yourself in the middle of a group of "wild things". This delightful classic is about the important things, like dancing in the moonlight and missing your mum.

title: White Teeth
author: Zadie Smith
description: This postcolonial novel focuses on the friendship of two wartime friends, a Bangladeshi and an Englishman. The story about mixed families, clashing ideologies and activism comes to a dramatic conclusion.

title: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?
author: Edward Albee
description: A play about two couples meeting for a late-night party that quickly deteriorates into snide jokes and volatile fighting as secrets from both couples are laid bare. A dark comedy criticising the American nuclear family and the pressures of social conformity.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: The only novel Emily Brontë ever wrote, and it's a masterpiece! A haunting tale of love and abuse set amidst the austere Yorkshire moors.

title: You've Reached Sam
author: Dustin Thao
description: When the 17-year-old Julie loses Sam, the shared future they imagined dies with him and everything changes. All she wants now is to hear his voice again when she calls his phone. And against all odds, it doesn't go to voicemail...

title: By Train Through Spain
author: Amerigo Marchesi
description: Join this charming and colourful journey across Spain with Amerigo Marchesi as they hop on trains, capture stunning vistas and uncover fascinating hidden gems.

title: Discovering the Greater Bookston Region
author: Peter Spinner
description: Join Peter Spinner as he looks for the well-kept hidden gems of the enchanting Greater Bookston Region. High-quality restaurants, cosy stays, endearing shops, and local events await!

title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 2
author: Ash Axbridge
description: Get ready for a mind-blowing journey through the wondrous world of knowledge! Volume 2 of Encyclopaedia Bookstonia: from D as in Detective Novels to J as in Japanese Manga.

title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 3
author: Ash Axbridge
description: Discover a world of knowledge and adventure in this thrilling third volume of Encyclopaedia Bookstonia. From K as in Knitting Instructions to O as in Omegaverse.

title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 4
author: Ash Axbridge
description: Another epic volume filled with knowledge and wonder! What else does this encyclopaedia series have in store? I'll tell you: Entries from P as in Philosophy to T as in True Crime.

title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 5
author: Ash Axbridge
description: Vol. 5 of this encyclopaedia concludes our journey of learning, with the entries we've all been waiting for: U as in Unfinished Manuscripts to Y as in Yuri. (They forgot to print Z).

title: The Encyclopedia of the Weird and Wonderful; Curious and Incredible Facts that Will Blow Your Mind
author: Milo Rossi
description: Our world and history is a complex and fascinating thing, and this collection of entertaining facts and stories helps humanize our past. From prehistory, ancient games, Pompeii, and more, each page holds an entertaining tale.

title: Finding Optimism; The Future Is Good
author: Liliane Renaud
description: Liliane Renaud believes that, despite everything, the future must be bright. This solarpunk-inspired work is packed with thoughtful poems and practical insights to guide you through life's most difficult challenges.

title: Herbcraft; The Power of Natural Healing and Hexing
author: Star Ravenhunt
description: Get ready to brew up some magic as Star Ravenhunt shares the secrets of herbcraft, from natural healing potions to delicious recipes to mischievous hexes.

title: Here Be Dragons; (Welsh Princes #1)
author: Sharon Kay Penman
description: The first in a trilogy of Medieval Fantasy Romance follows the tale of Joanna - the illegitimate daughter of King John - as she finds herself choosing between loyalty and love.

title: Historical Niche
author: Terry Czernik
description: This in-depth exploration of the Danelaw by a scholar of history promises sophisticated insights for anyone with an interest in 886–1066 AD in Northern England.

title: HTML 1998; An Introdcution
author: Hello Worldly
description: Get ready to enter the digital world with this 90s guide to HTML (specifically 3.2), the language that powers the internet. Let's say "Hello, World!"

title: In Search Of:; The Most Beautiful Islands In the World
author: Je Hyun
description: The newest entry in our In Search Of series: A marvellous view across stunning islands, where paradise awaits at every turn, even if you're on a budget.

title: Just A Story: Why We Still Tell Fairytales
author: Isabel Galvan
description: Once upon a time... there was the captivating world of fairytales. Discover why these timeless tales continue to enchant and intrigue us in this cultural and anthropological study.

title: Kitchen Rules For Your Family and You
author: Mbwana Jones
description: Spice up your family's kitchen adventures with this delightful guide. From cooking tips to family bonding, discover the recipe for a happy home!

title: Know My Name
author: Chanel Miller
description: In the news, she was known only as Emily Doe. Chanel's experience, an example of the justice system failing the most vulnerable, went viral after her victim impact statement was posted on Buzzfeed. A powerful memoir told in uniquely beautiful prose.

title: Living In Alaska
author: Sioned Jones
description: This chilling page-turner, based on Jones' true story, will take you on a wild journey through the frozen wilderness of Alaska, filled with heartbreak, resilience, and unexpected turns.

title: The Long Unwinding Road; A Journey through the Heart of Wales
author: Marc P Jones
description: Come with Marc P Jones as he takes you through the beautiful green hills and valleys of Wales. Discover Wales' deep majesty and ancient history, with local voices at the fore.

title: Medieval Carpentry
author: Obu Henderson
description: Woodworking tips and tricks from the days of knights and castles. Unearth ancient techniques and bring medieval craftsmanship back to life!

title: Mesopotamian Buildings
author: Ahmed Mansour
description: Discover the awe-inspiring marvels crafted by ancient hands in this fascinating delve into Mesopotamian architecture. Join us on a journey through time!

title: Physics 1908
author: Kendra Conelli
description: Discover the captivating world of physics through a historical journey that will tickle your brain and transport you to 1908.

title: Round Luxembourg with Brooke
author: Brooke Dixon
description: Join rising Instagram star BrookeTravels on an adventure through Luxembourg as she explores, shares delicious recipes, and provides a refreshing take on travel and lifestyle.

title: Round the World in Eighty Dishes
author: Lesley Blanch
description: A rich collection of dishes from around the world, each accompanied by its own travel anecdote that opens a fascinating window into a time long past.

title: St. Bookston: The Myth, the Legend, the Truth
author: H. A. Pennington
description: The most brilliant writer and philosopher of his time. But who was he really? And why do we know so little about his life? Finally uncover the truth in this groundbreaking investigative biography.

title: The Debvoir Family; A Success Story
author: Kennedy Naybon
description: Follow the triumphs and trials of a remarkable family, as the Debvoir clan shapes and is challenged by the very history of Bookstonbury.

title: Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen
author: Olympe de Gouges
description: "Woman has the right to mount the scaffold, she must equally have the right to mount the rostrum [speaking platform]." French Revolutionary Olympe de Gouges flips the male-only Declaration of Human Rights, in this fearless and witty manifesto for gender equality.

title: Top 50 Camper Van Destinations
author: Tamir Ghasti
description: From winding coastal roads to serene mountain retreats, this comprehensive camping guide unveils a collection of breathtaking landscapes and hidden gems.

title: Topdog/Underdog
author: Suzan-Lori Parks
description: Booth wants to be as good at three-card monte as his older brother Lincoln, who's sworn off the hustling life. Money's tight, and Lincoln's honest work isn't going to get them far, as this one-room play explores the intersection of race, poverty, and brotherhood.

title: Traditional Building Techniques
author: Lohar Bishmal
description: Have you ever looked at an old city's houses, castles and bridges and asked yourself: "How did they build that"? This book illustrates the greatest building techniques of all time and what we can learn from them today.

title: A Clash of Kings
author: George R. R. Martin
description: The 2nd volume in the ASOIAF series continues to deliver the most heart-wrenching twists and tragedies of medieval fantasy: mysteries of parentage, magic, murder, war, and epic adventures all throughout the lands of Westeros.

title: The Code Book; The Science of Secrecy from Ancient Egypt to Quantum Cryptography
author: Simon Singh
description: Crack codes, unravel secrets, and explore gripping historical mysteries. From ancient ciphers to World War II's Enigma, Singh invites you to learn cryptography and test your skills with real code-breaking exercises.

title: A Court of Mist and Fury
author: Sarah J. Maas
description: Get ready for a sexy, epic and twisting book two in the ACOTAR series, where the immortal drama of the fae unfolds around haunted protagonist Feyre. Will she find the right side to stand with?

title: The Cream Tea Killer
author: Judy Leigh
description: Amateaur sleuth Morwenna is looking forward to a bit of normality, until the local DJ she was supposed to be meeting washes up at the beach. Despite being dubbed The Cream Tea Killer , they are anything but sweet and it is up to Morwenna to unmask them.

title: A Feast for Crows
author: George R. R. Martin
description: The war for the Iron Throne seems to have burned itself out to a truce... for now. But it wouldn't be A Song of Ice and Fire without some deceit, ambitious plotting, power struggles, and mysterious sorcery at work.

title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
author: William Shakespeare
description: Simple love triangles are for beginners. In this classic play, romantic entanglements involve four young, love-sick Greeks, fae royalty, enchantment spells, and a donkey, resulting in a comedy for the ages.

title: Walden
author: Henry David Thoreau
description: Ever wanted to walk away from civilization, into the woods, and owe nothing to anyone but yourself? You'll find a friend in Henry David Thoreau. His record of simple living and contemplation of civil disobedience will fascinate nature-lovers and deep thinkers alike.

title: A Walk in the Woods
author: Bill Bryson
description: The tale of two men in their forties, with countless blisters and a questionable map, on the Appalachian Trail. Get to know the area's history, ecology, and people in this hilarious exploration of the great outdoors.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
description: Follow a curious girl as she tumbles down the rabbit hole, into a world filled with talking animals and puzzling adventures. A classic tale of nonsense and whimsy, illustrated by John Tenniel.

title: All My Sons
author: Arthur Miller
description: Set in the Midwest after WWII, this play is a fragmented family drama and tragedy. A father and son, a forbidden romance, unpunished crimes, and a dark secret that threatens to tear the characters apart.

title: All Out; The No-Longer-Secret Stories of Queer Teens throughout the Ages
author: Various Authors
description: An anthology of Queer historical fiction, telling captivating and emotive stories which take you on a journey through history. Experience a diverse range of identities, stories, and cultures in this vibrant expression of queer history.

title: All She Was Worth
author: Miyuki Miyabe
description: How desperate is a person who steals another's identity? Detective Honma searches for his nephew's missing fiancée, unravelling grim crimes to uncover the true Shoko since the dead leave traces in the living.

title: All Systems Red; The Murderbot Diaries #1
author: Martha Wells
description: Meet Murderbot, a SecUnit who recently hacked their governor chip. Too bad it keeps getting sent on planetary bodyguard contracts for the shady Company! All this android wants is space to have an existential crisis and binge-watch their favourite program.

title: All Your Twisted Secrets
author: Diana Urban
description: Six high school teenagers meet up under false pretenses and are locked in a room with only one direction: before the hour is up, they must choose one person to die. Amidst the chaos that ensues, a second question rises: who did this to them?

title: All's Well That Ends Well
author: William Shakespeare
description: Sometimes, a happy ending can be a woman getting the man she wanted, even if he's generally quite unpleasant. Shakespearean drama and confusion as it should be.

title: Allegiant; Divergent #3
author: Veronica Roth
description: As the Factionless seize power, a new civil war threatens to destroy what remains of the shattered faction society. Tris, Four, and a handful of allies must venture beyond the barriers to save their city from self-destruction. How is the war going to end? And when?

title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold
author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
description: In this heartwarming and thought-provoking story, a cosy cafe in Tokyo has a mysterious twist... Can you change the past, or will the coffee get cold before you do?

title: Belinda
author: Maria Edgeworth
description: Belinda has aspirations beyond London's social season. Amongst the heroine's witty observations of eighteenth-century society, this novel also touches on the challenging issues of feminism, racism, and obsession. One of Jane Austen's favourite books!

title: Beowulf
author: Unknown, transl. by S. Heaney
description: An Old English epos that still puzzles scholars to this day. Who can we credit for this poetic tale of a Scandinavian folk hero? When was it written? And how much does it tell us about our history?

title: The Best Short Stories of O. Henry
author: O. Henry, B. Cerf & V.H. Cartmell
description: 38 tales from an American writer famous for surprise endings! Will Porter began writing short stories from prison in 1898. He later changed his name and started fresh in New York City. He wrote over 600 stories in his lifetime. Some aged better than others.

title: Blood of Elves; (The Witcher)
author: Andrzej Sapkowski
description: After the success of previous short stories, the Polish fantasy series now takes off into its first novel, wherein the magically gifted Ciri must flee from her war-torn home, and comes under the protection of Geralt of Rivia.

title: Blood, Sweat, and Pixels
author: Jason Schreier
description: Jason Schreier, documents how ten famous video games were developed by interviewing their developers retrospectively. These real stories of dedication, hope, suffering, and frustration reveal the intricacies of the game industry.

title: The Blue Castle
author: L.M. Montgomery
description: When 29-year-old Valancy gets bad news from her doctor, she decides she’s ready to live. She’s done letting her family dictate how she spends her days, and she offers friendship to the townsfolk they despise. A romantic and hopeful novel about second chances.

title: Blue Highways; The Travel Trilogy #1
author: William Least Heat-Moon
description: William set off on what would become a 13,000 mile journey by van, visiting the most overlooked small towns in America. His series of travel memoirs prove that it's not where you go, it's who you meet! Blue highways are back roads.

title: Blue Sisters
author: Coco Mellors
description: After their sister’s death, three wildly different siblings return to New York to save their childhood home and face the truths they’ve long avoided. A moving, sharp story of grief, identity, and the ties that bind.

title: Carrie
author: Stephen King
description: A classic of dark teen horror. High schooler Carrie White is mercilessly bullied by her peers and abused by her religious mother. But when an especially cruel prank is used to humiliate her, her latent telekinetic powers know no bounds.

title: Case Closed; One and the Same? (Vol. 3)
author: Gosho Aoyama
description: When 17yo superstar detective Shinichi Kudo follows the wrong people, he's poisoned and turns back into a kid! Now as grade schooler Conan Edogawa, he still solves cases, this time on a cruise ship, in this famous whodunnit Manga series.

title: Catching Fire
author: Suzanne Collins
description: The cycle established in the dystopian society of Panem continues. The brutal Hunger Games are held again, and traumatised Katniss and Peeta get no choice but to play along, and fight not only for their survival, but also for a revolution...

title: Cats in Space... and Other Places
author: Various Authors
description: Love Cats? Love Spaces? You'll love this. Revel in feline supremacy while reading tales by the likes of Ursula Le Guin, Arthur C. Clarke and Anne McCaffrey. Approved by Freya!

title: Caturday in Bookstonbury; Volume 2
author: Luna Knight
description: In this visual photographic history of Bookstonbury, Luna Knight documents the local feline population. From majestic longhairs to playful shorthairs and everything in between, take a gander and learn more about these adorable floofs.

title: The Caucasian Chalk Circle
author: Bertolt Brecht
description: A play-within-a-play culminating in a trial to decide if a boy should go to the rich woman who gave birth to him or the maid who raised him. A piece of Epic Theatre which delivers political themes of justice, class inequality, and the aftermath of war.

title: Cemetery Boys
author: Aiden Thomas
description: A trans teen determined to prove to his Latinx family that he’s a brujo tries to summon his cousin’s spirit to solve his death, but ends up instead with a ridiculously handsome ghost. A hauntingly cute paranormal romance and mystery perfect for spooky season.

title: Chain-Gang All-Stars
author: Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah
description: For nearly three years, Loretta has fought and killed, hoping to win her own freedom. Told in multiple perspectives, this brutal dystopian novel highlights the horrors of the US prison system and society's obsession with reality entertainment.

title: The Chalk Man
author: C.J. Tudor
description: In 1986, Eddie and his friends used chalk figures as a secret code—until it led them to a body. Now in 2016, these menacing figures have returned, and another murder ensues. Eddie must return to the past to uncover seething secrets and unearth the killer's identity.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Poverty and guilt drive a bright young man to a dark deed. How will he grapple with the consequences of his crime?

title: Critical Hits; Writers on Gaming and the Alternate Worlds We Inhabit
author: Various Authors
description: An anthology of personal essays by multiple published authors exploring their relationship with video games that affected them deeply, Learn about the transformative world of games and how they shape our lives.

title: The CRPG Book; Guide to Computer Role-Playing Games
author: Collection
description: This encyclopedia tells the history of computer role-playing games by listing all CRPG titles released up to 2020 in chronological order. You can see how games influenced each other and role-playing practices, both in digital and tabletop settings.

title: Don Quixote
author: Miguel de Cervantes
description: A mad "knight" embarks on hilarious adventures with his faithful, not-so-bright sidekick in this classic satire.

title: Don't Let the Forest In
author: C.G. Drews
description: A gothic high school, a haunted writer, a secretive artist. Andrew and Thomas must fight back the monstrosities born from the art they created, while their feeling for each other grow tangled and wild.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: An epic saga of intergalactic politics and precious resources, where one young man finds himself surrounded by inhospitable desert, and at the centre of a messianic prophecy.

title: East of Eden
author: John Steinbeck
description: A retelling of Genesis set on California farmland in 1865. This complex novel centers on the timeless struggles of two families, exploring themes of rivalry, identity, and love.

title: Edinburgh; Picturesque Notes
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: A travelogue told in a series of anecdotes with whimsical exaggerations that capture the author's view of his hometown circa late 1870s, in all its glories and infamies.

title: The Eleventh Hour; A Curious Mystery
author: Graeme Base
description: Horace the elephant invites his friends to celebrate his eleventh birthday with a feast, only to discover that it has been eaten at the eleventh hour! Can you find the hidden messages and solve the mystery of who ate the birthday feast?

title: Elsewhere; One Woman, One Rucksack, One Lifetime of Travel
author: Rosita Boland
description: Rosita reflects on the life-changing experiences and people she met on nine journeys, from a chaotic bus ride in Pakistan to a healing swim in Bali, carrying only a rucksack and a diary.  An emotion-filled collection of essays, both thrilling and heartbreaking.

title: Fire & Blood
author: George R. R. Martin
description: Finally, an even more historical fantasy novel, from the world of Ice and Fire. Wherein all the messy relationships, wars, and secrets of the royal Targaryen dynasty are aired out.

title: Frank Lloyd Wright
author: Frank Lloyd Wright
description: From prairie houses to the Guggenheim museum, this architect had range! This wonderful coffee table book is jam-packed with sketches and photographs for all architecture enjoyers.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: Oh, to be 18 again, and write a masterpiece over a particularly cold and dark summer holiday, unknowingly laying the very foundation of our modern horror fiction. Wish that were me.

title: Ghost Stories; From the Grave
author: Collection
description: Prepare to be chilled to the bone as you journey into the realm of the supernatural with this collection of eerie and haunting tales. With Dickens, Stoker, Wilde, and Poe, as well as new stories.

title: Great Big Beautiful Life
author: Emily Henry
description: Two writers. One legendary subject. Alice wants her big break. Hayden wants everyone to leave him alone. Instead, they're trapped on an island competing for the same biography, juggling cryptic stores, ironclad NDAs, and an attraction neither of them requested.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
description: A classic Dickens! Poverty, morality, smelly cities, and unjust austerity measures lead to a rags-to-riches extravaganza with a lot of heartbreak on the way. Oh, right, I forgot orphans.

title: Heinemann Mathematics
author: Scottish Primary Mathematics Group
description: The classic textbook for everyone's favourite subject in school! Packed with all the greatest hits like arithmetic, trigonometry, and stochastics.

title: How Winston Delivered Christmas; A Christmas Story in Twenty-Four-and-a-Half Chapters
author: Alex T. Smith
description: A brave little mouse sets off on a quest to deliver a lost letter to Father Christmas on Christmas Eve. This picture book is designed to be read as an Advent calendar, and includes activities for children impatiently counting down the days till Christmas.

title: Howl, and Other Poems
author: Allen Ginsberg
description: There are nice poems, and then there are those tried by the law in an obscenity trial: Radical, honest, political, soft, holy. And life-changing. I much prefer the latter category.

title: I Capture the Castle
author: Dodie Smith
description: Seventeen year-old Cassandra lives in the remnants of a castle with her eccentric family. Her 1934 journal is going strong, but her father's latest book is a work-in-procrastination, so money is tight. Maybe romance and a strategic prank can change their fates!

title: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
author: Maya Angelou
description: Maya's childhood was one of prejudice, neglect, and violence. Adult Maya finds the keys to her cage of trauma through self-love, escaping to the embrace of good books and kind people. A tragic and inspiring autobiography from a resilient Black poet.

title: I, Robot
author: Isaac Asimov
description: This set of nine delightful short stories imagine a world of robot and human colaboration and explores some interesting concepts within this framing. A foundational text of modern Sci-Fi, and a must read in the storebought version of the future we ended up in.

title: If Beale Street Could Talk
author: James Baldwin
description: Tish and Fonny are engaged and expecting a child, when Fonny is jailed for a crime he didn't commit. Their families band together to try to clear his name. An emotionally devastating love story about racial prejudice and criminal injustice.

title: If Tomorrow Comes
author: Sidney Sheldon
description: A thrilling mystery about a regular woman's descent into a life of crime. Betrayed by love and framed by the mafia, Tracy has to fight back to survive.

title: Inkheart
author: Cornelia Funke
description: Pen and paper can bring characters to life, but what happens when they escape the page? The beginning of a fantastical and dangerous adventure into the world of a book, for all ages.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: This intimately narrated story of the winding life of Jane Eyre touches on many social issues present in Victorian England. Her story is frought with twists and hardships but ultimately leads to love.

title: Jean Dubuffet
author: Jean Dubuffet
description: Explore the fascinating world of French artist, Jean Debuffet. Learn how he strived to thwart conventional standards of beauty in favour of more authentic and humanistic ways of image making.

title: Henry VI, Part 1
author: William Shakespeare
description: Watch as personal squabbles, petty jealousy and Joan of Arc tear apart the English political system in this first part of Shakespeare's King Henry VI trilogy.

title: Henry VI, Part 3
author: William Shakespeare
description: This final part of Shakespeare's King Henry VI trilogy focuses on the horrors that ensued during the Wars of the Roses as the nation is thrown into chaos and morality makes way for revenge.

title: Richard II
author: William Shakespeare
description: Shakespeare's classic historical drama about the downfall of King Richard the Second, complete with scheming nobles and history-defining power politics.

title: Legendborn; The Legendborn Cycle #1
author: Tracy Deonn
description: A magical story about black women and pain through generations. In this twist on King's Arthur's legend, Bree struggles to find out why she is the only one who can resist the effects of magic and how the secret order she infiltrates relates to her mother's death.

title: Les Miserables
author: Victor Hugo
description: 19th-century Paris. A man running from the law just wants a chance to live his life. Injustice is everywhere. But resistance is brewing, and love is not far. Don't expect anyone to sing, or you'll be disappointed.

title: Letters from Egypt; 1862-1869
author: Lucie Duff Gordon
description: After her diagnosis of tuberculosis, Lady Gordon travels to Egypt in hopes of improving her dwindling health. A compilation of her letters, detailing her account of life in Luxor, this is the story of an Englishwoman's immersion into Egyptian culture.

title: Letters of Bookstonbury
author: Allatheena Jeon
description: After her grandmother's death, a quiet librarian inherits a mobile bookshop. She plans to sell it - until she finds a hidden compartment beneath the floorboards, with old, unsent letters addressed to people all over town, uncovering stories of love, loss, and hope.

title: The Library Book
author: Susan Orlean
description: A journalist's engaging investigation into the 1986 fire at the Los Angeles Public Library. Part true-crime story, part essay on what libraries mean to us, and why the burning of books or libraries is so devastating

title: The Long Way to a Small Angry Planet; Wayfarers #1
author: Becky Chambers
description: In this queer space opera, a rag-tag team of travelers take a dangerous job tunnelling a wormhole to a distant planet. The commission of a lifetime might not pay off, but the found-family in this sci-fi series sure does!

title: Looking for Alaska
author: John Green
description: Boarding school is not what Miles thought it was gonna be. And neither is that girl he meets, Alaska. Together they search for the meaning behind last words, in this young adult story.

title: Lord of the Flies
author: William Golding
description: A group of school boys is suddenly stranded on a remote island. Will they manage to survive without any grownups, or will they succumb to their darker instincts?

title: A Man for All Seasons
author: Robert Bolt
description: This biographical dramatization follows the escalating conflict between Lor Chancellor Sir Thomas More and Henry VIII from 1529 to 1535. As Henry pushes political and religious buttons, More pushes back. A historical play that will leave you wanting more.

title: Maria Stuart
author: Friedrich Schiller
description: A Tudor tale of power, betrayal, and queens. Witness the captivating drama and heart-wrenching decisions of a regal Mary, in this loveletter to Shakespearian plays by a legendary German playwright.

title: Matilda
author: Roald Dahl
description: A mischievous little genius delights in books and uses her powers to outsmart nasty grown-ups. Will she make it through the school system in one piece?

title: A Matter of Oaths
author: Helen S. Wright
description: When memory-wiped Rafe applies for a job on a random patrol ship, a world-changing space opera unfolds: space battles, secret identities, queer romance, and VR tech only the 80s could imagine.

title: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
author: Ransom Riggs
description: More than just peculiar, these children seem downright supernatural! Follow along this haunting adventure about found family and not fitting in, illustrated with vintage photography.

title: Mont-Saint-Michel and Chartres
author: Henry Adams
description: A fictional travelogue, self-described as "not anything that can possibly be useful or instructive — but only a sense of what those centuries had to say, and a sympathy with their ways of saying it."

title: Mother Night
author: Kurt Vonnegut
description: An American in Germany turned spy during World War II, is facing trial as a Nazi war criminal. Does the vital role he inadvertently played in the Nazi propaganda machine make him guilty?

title: The Mousetrap and Other Plays
author: Agatha Christie
description: A locked room mystery in a snowbound bed and breakfast by The Queen of Crime. The Mousetrap opened at the Theatre Royal in Nottingham, England on October 6, 1952. The play met with such success it didn't leave the stage in 70 years, becoming history's longest running play.

title: Mrs. Dalloway
author: Virginia Woolf
description: Get to know Clarissa as she prepares for a party later that evening. Learn about her life and meet her guests while pondering human nature and exploring the social structures of the 1920s. Will her party be a success?

title: Much Ado About Nothing
author: William Shakespeare
description: A web of love, lies and misunderstandings encircle four lovers. Laugh along as their lives get turned upside down in this punny romp about jealousy and trust.

title: Night and Day
author: Virginia Woolf
description: Can love and marriage coexist and is marriage necessary for happiness? Explore love and life in Edwardian London as night and day contrast just as the lives of Katherine and Mary.

title: Night Sky with Exit Wounds
author: Ocean Vuong
description: This collection of poetry courageously explores violence and the delicacy of life. The author tells of the Vietnam War, of his experience with 9/11, and of queer love.

title: On Beauty
author: Zadie Smith
description: Follow the increasingly intertwining lives of two very different academic families as their ideologies clash and their struggle with black identity and the nature of beauty unfolds.

title: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous
author: Ocean Vuong
description: A novel written in the form of a letter, addressed from a son to his illiterate mother; a recipient who, like a ghost, is not promised - only longed for. Redolent of queer and feminist thinking, this is a raw and earnest exploration of race, class, and honesty.

title: Orlando
author: Virginia Woolf
description: A medley through over three centuries of history, featuring a suave protagonist and lots of moments of self-discovery. Filled with passionate affairs, bittersweet moments, bending the rules of time, class, and gender.

title: Othello
author: William Shakespeare
description: The heroic black general Othello soon finds himself in the middle of intrigue and betrayal after one fateful promotion. The start of a brutal tragedy about someone who “loved not wisely but too well”.

title: P.S. I Still Love You
author: Jenny Han
description: In this bittersweet sequel to a YA bestseller, the turbulent romance continues. A gripping story with lots of twists and turns, beautiful moments, betrayals, and a charged game of Assassins.

title: Pageboy
author: Elliot Page
description: This memoir details Page's journey of self-discovery, and of overcoming the many hurdles put up by a transphobic and misogynistic film industry, to get to where he is now.

title: Parable of the Sower
author: Octavia E. Butler
description: In a dystopian world ravaged by climate change and corporate greed, a young woman embarks on a biblical journey to spread the seeds of a new religion in an attempt to redeem humanity.

title: Persepolis; The Story of a Childhood
author: Marjane Satrapi
description: A visually stunning and bold graphic novel memoir following a young Iranian girl through the 1970s and 1980s. This gripping story explores themes of revolution, religion, family, history and daily life in the face of tumultuous times.

title: Peter Pan in Kensington Gardens
author: J. M. Barrie
description: A story about a mischivious boy who becomes stuck "Betwixt-and-Between" childhood and growing up, between the real world and the magical world of Kensington Gardens after dark.

title: Prince Caspian; The Return to Narnia
author: C.S. Lewis
description: In this second installment of the Chronicles of Narnia series our protagonists suddenly return to a changed Narnia, and must help their friends defeat an evil despot making a play for power.

title: The Princess Bride
author: William Goldman
description: This fantasy story contains: battles of wit, feats of strength, rodents of unusual size, sword fights of revenge, and the truest of true love, all saturated with inconceivable levels of satire.

title: Saga; Volume 9
author: Brian K. Vaughan & Fiona Staples
description: Star Wars meets Game of Thrones! This ninth entry in the Saga series of graphic novels explores fake news and genuine terror in an epic sci-fi setting. Prepare for a heart-warming tale full of tragic twists.

title: Scott Pilgrim's Precious Little Life (#1)
author: Bryan Lee O'Malley
description: A quirky graphic novel about a nonchalant slacker turned romantic hero who must defeat his crush's seven evil exes. It's a pretty clever metaphor for feeling insecure about your new partners romantic past, or so I am told.

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Jane Austen
description: A tale of two sisters, romantic engagements, quarrels, and the difficulty of making sensible and sensual choices in matters of love and marriage of course. Austen's delightful wit and sharp characterizations are great as ever in this all-time classic.

title: Sister Outsider
author: Audre Lorde
description: A collection of boundary-breaking essays and speeches in which author Audre Lorde negotiates her complex identity as a Black woman, lesbian, poet, activist, cancer survivor, mother, and feminist.

title: Starstruck; (Deluxe Edition)
author: Elaine Lee & Michael Kaluta
description: It’s a tough galaxy out there, but somebody's gotta live in it, and it might as well be YOU! The brilliant, feminist, sci-fi play turned graphic novel that you may not have heard of yet.

title: Stormbreaker
author: Anthony Horowitz
description: Ever dreamt of becoming a teenage spy for MI6 and uncovering a nefarious plot? The plot may be a little ridiculous but you probably won't care as you race along this thrilling first entry in the Alex Rider series.

title: Sula
author: Toni Morrison
description: The story of the friendship between two young Black girls and the conflicting paths that their lives take them on. Read on as their opposing personalities affect the town in a tale about defying social norms, resentment and reconciliation.

title: The Sunlit Man
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: Nomad has been jumping between different worlds to stay ahead of his pursuers. But with his diminished powers, he is trapped on a planet where the sun's intensity will kill, and finds himself caught up in a struggle between a despotic ruler and the defiant rebels.

title: Supernova; Renegades #3
author: Marissa Meyer
description: The Renegades' greatest enemy is alive, a danger once more to Gatlon City. In this thrilling conclusion to the Renegades , Adrian and Nova struggle to protect those they love, all while keeping secrets from one another. When the dust settles, who will be left standing?

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Join the brilliant detective and his loyal companion on thrilling investigations as they unravel mysteries and outwit criminals in 12 legendary tales.

title: The Book of Tea
author: Okakura Kakuzo
description: An open letter to the west, learn all about the Japanese values of Teaism and let them enrich your life. One of the great English tea classics that bridges the gap between the spritual and secular spheres of tea.

title: The Book of the City of Ladies
author: Christine de Pizan
description: Guided by three allegorical figures, a woman builds a symbolic city with walls protecting women from slander and misogyny, celebrating their courage, wisdom, and achievements - radically ahead of its time in 15th-century Europe.

title: Book of Yokai ; Mysterious Creatures of Japanese Folklore
author: Michael Dylan Foster & Shinonome Kijin
description: Yokai is a shorthand for all fantastical beings and supernatural phenomena in Japanese stories. This folkloric encyclopaedia is filled with their origins and meanings.

title: The Canterbury Tales
author: Geoffrey Chaucer
description: Twenty-four stories told by twenty-four pilgrims as they travel to Canterbury Cathedral. Who can tell the most enthralling one and win a free meal at the Tabard Inn? This classic piece of English literature has been thought to have popularized the language in mainstream literature, but was it ever finished?

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
description: In this epic tale of revenge, redemption, and exquisite French drama, a betrayed lover returns to the Parisian high society in search of sweet revenge.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: An unlikely band of heroes must go on a quest to destroy an evil ring once and for all. Their journey through Tolkien's vibrant fantasy world has become part of the foundation of modern fantasy literature.

title: The Girl Who Played with Fire
author: Stieg Larsson
description: This book must be one of the darkest Nordic crime thrillers out there. Still, Larsson manages to sneak in moments of kindness and allyship that make this brutal revenge epos just barely possible to endure.

title: The Green Ember; Book 1
author: S.D. Smith & Zach Franzen
description: Forced to flee their home, siblings Heather and Picket come to a hidden refuge where each rabbit trains their gifts to bring about a Mended Wood. Kids will love this series with its brave characters and themes of found family. Rabbits with swords!

title: The Green Mile
author: Stephen King
description: The heart-wrenching story of a death-row inmate with magical abilities. Prepare for a sordid tale of a corrupt and cruel institution and of the mouse that survived it all.

title: Greenglass House; Book 1
author: Kate Milford & Jaime Zollars
description: Milo has plans to exclusively munch on cookies and read books during his winter holidays. But thanks to a snow storm, his parents' inn fills with guests, all strangely invested in the story of their house. A locked room mystery and a treasure hunt, with a surprise twist!

title: The Gunslinger
author: Stephen King
description: The last gunslinger's treacherous search for his ancient adversary leads him across an alternate reality Old West. A path full of monsters, demons and sacrifice lead to his ultimate destination: The Dark Tower.

title: The House with a Clock in Its Walls
author: John Bellairs
description: A ticking time-clock threatens to destroy the world. A newbie and a local boy team up to stop the magical doomsday plot. Join them in this illustrated romp full of black magic, ghosts and derring-do.

title: How Did Whales Get So Big?; An Other Curious Questions about Animals, Nature, Geology and Planet Earth
author: MinuteEarth
description: Are you a child who can't stop asking questions like, "Why did my hamster eat her babies?" Try this kid-friendly encyclopaedia! Filled with stick-figure illustrations and rigorous research., this STEM book is perfect for answering even the most curious kid's questions.

title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
author: C. S. Lewis
description: In this delightful classic siblings stumble upon a magical world through an ordinary wardrobe, where talking animals and a wicked witch await.

title: Listen for the Lie
author: Amy Tintera
description: Lucy doesn't want to be on a podcast about her best friend's murder. Her memory from that night is sketchy at best, and the town has already decided who's guilty. But true crime podcaster Ben is both persistent and attractive. Unputdownable and spicy!

title: The Lost Continent
author: C. J. Cutcliffe Hyne
description: Classic fantasy meets greek mythology in this 1972 retelling of the legend of Atlantis. A heroic warrior priest is all that stands between an avaricious empress and the end of an era.

title: The Odyssey
author: Homer, transl. by Knox & Fagles
description: A legendary Greek epos about a perilous journey home, with many mythical roadblocks along the way. Good thing, our protagonist is smart as a whip, and nobody is able to stop him.

title: Oh, Mary!
author: Cole Escola
description: In this play, all Mary Todd Lincoln wants to do is star in a cabaret and drink, but instead she is forced to stay cooped up in Washington, DC, while her husband deals with the Civil War. Desperate to distract her, Abe hires an acting coach to give her lessons on the stage

title: Olivetti
author: Allie Millington
description: When its human family is in crisis, a vintage typewriter breaks the rules to communicate what they most need to remember. A heartfelt and beautiful middle-grade book!

title: The Outsider
author: Stephen King
description: The terrifying Outsider stalks Flint City, committing heinous crimes. Tag along a rag-tag team of heroes who take it upon themselves to deal with this nightmare in classic Stephen King fashion.

title: The Poetry of Architecture
author: John Ruskin
description: Perhaps the origins of cottage core? John Ruskin will take you on a tour of his favourite cottages and villas throughout Europe. Delight in his philosophical musings about the beautiful interplay of nature and architecture.

title: Pollyanna; Book 1
author: Eleanor H. Porter
description: A little orphan girl with toxic positivity moves in with her cold matronly Aunt, and winds up changing the entire mood of their small town in Vermont. A classic book that inspired hundreds of children to start 'gladness clubs' ( Yes, really ).

title: The Return of the King
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: The legendary showdown between good and evil, bravery and cowardice, love and doubt in a fantasy world on the brink of collapse. In between it all are some of the most poetic character moments in writing history.

title: The Scarecrow of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
description: Return to the land of Oz and embark on a typically Ozian adventure lined with quirky characters and unlikely scenarios. Join Cap'n Bill, Trot and a magical Scarecrow as they take down dastardly King Krewl.

title: The Shadow of the Wind
author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
description: He possesses the only known copy of a mysterious book by an even more mysterious author. Join Daniel on his treacherous journey to uncover the story of the book and its author in this winding neo-gothic novel.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
description: A terrifying delve into the twisted mind of Alicia Berenson. What moved her to suddenly murder her husband? And will the search for the truth be too much to bear...

title: The Snowy Day
author: Ezra Jack Keats
description: A young Black boy explores his neighbourhood transformed by the magic of snow. The beautiful illustrations of this charming story helped pave the way for more inclusive representation in children's literature.

title: So Easy So Good
author: Kylie Sakaida
description: Packed with recipes and information on healthy eating, this cookbook draws from Kylie's expertise as a Japanese-American dietician to make cooking accessible, practical and delicious for all.

title: Stone Butch Blues
author: Leslie Feinberg
description: A butch lesbian comes of age in the world of gay bars, homophobic police raids, and her complex relationship to gender. While unflinching in its depiction of homophobic violence, this book has some of the most achingly romantic prose about love you'll ever read.

title: The Stones of Venice
author: John Ruskin
description: A thoroughly researched exploration of Venitian art and architecture, comprised of three groundbreaking volumes. If you have a soft spot for hard rocks, get this!

title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: In this fantastic gothic horror thriller not everything is as it seems, when a violent madman begins an escalating crime spree in London. As a lawyer begins investigating these mysterious incidents, a brilliant exploration of identities and dark urges ensues.

title: The Two Towers
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: In this second book in Tolkien's foundational fantasy epic, the forces of evil have not been idle, and so our protagonists see themselves surrounded by evil creatures and poor advisors.

title: The Westing Game
author: Ellen Raskin
description: 16 heirs must pair up to solve the mystery of eccentric millionaire Sam Westing's last will and testament, all to win his vast fortune. Puzzle along as the twist and turns of this clever case unfold.

title: Towards a New Architecture
author: Le Corbusier
description: This polarizing manifesto calls for a new architecture for modern times. A foundational text to understand Corbusier's work, brutalism and mid-century architectural movements.

title: Ugly Love
author: Colleen Hoover
description: He doesn't want love, and she doesn't have time for it. Sounds like a perfect arrangement with benefits, right? If only people and their hearts were so simple...

title: Understanding Comics; The Invisible Art
author: Scott McCloud
description: This book makes you appreciate both creating and reading comics as a hobby even more! By going over the history of visual storytelling, it explains how design choices - often invisible to readers' eyes - affect the reading experience.

title: The Unexpected Mrs. Pollifax; Mrs. Pollifax #1
author: Dorothy Gilman
description: Emily Pollifax is a widowed empty-nester who's always dreamt of becoming a spy. So at 60 years of age, she leaves her tiny apartment in New Jersey to visit Washington, and ask politely if the CIA will have her. Thus begins a hilarious and lighthearted mystery series!

title: White Night
author: Jim Butcher
description: Wizard detective Harry Dresden is back in the 9th instalment of The Dresden Files. His new case takes him into Chicago's seedy underbelly as he tracks a vicious serial killer of magical practitioners.

title: Witch Wood
author: John Buchan
description: The devil lurks in the Witch Wood, or so people say. A disappearing minister, a satanic cult and a ravaging plague, but what lies at the bottom of it all? Find out in this Scottish masterpiece.

title: Z for Zachariah
author: Robert C. O'Brian
description: When her brother left the valley and didn't return, Ann assumed that she was the last survivor of a nuclear war. That is, until a stranger in a radiation suit appeared. Why was he here? What did he want? A thrilling tale of survival and not knowing who to trust.

title: Zaha Hadid
author: Zaha Hadid
description: Concrete, light, curves! This coffee table book is packed with some of contemporary architecture's finest works by visionary architect Zaha Hadid.

title: Adventures of A Wild Child
author: Gina Grayson Hunt
description: Join the escapades of a free-spirited wanderer as they navigate love, self-discovery, and countless adventures in this captivating memoir.

title: An Explorer's Guide to Georgetown
author: Zheng Greene
description: Discover the secrets of Georgetown in this fun and beautifully illustrated guide. Explore its history, indulge in local cuisine, and soak up the vibrant lifestyle.

title: An Unkindness of Ghosts
author: Rivers Solomon
description: On a deeply stratified spaceship, Aster uses her wit and courage to defy oppression. An afrofuturist, queer, and fiercely feminist journey.

title: Catching Carps
author: Nigel Carpum
description: Reel in this absolute catch of a book, because Carpum's fishing trip is something special! Weaving together carp facts, personal philosophy, and globetrotting tales, the author shares all his wisdom.

title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 1
author: Ash Axbridge
description: Discover a treasure trove of knowledge in this captivating encyclopaedia! From A as in Academia to C as in Crime, learn more about what makes the world of books go round.

title: Gemology: A Study in Ruby
author: Ellie Obsidia
description: Unearth the secrets of the dazzling gemstones in this sparkling study of gemology. A challenging academic text from an expert of the field.

title: The Ghost Map; A Street, a City, An Epidemic and the Hidden Power of Urban Networks
author: Steven Johnson
description: Two different paths converge, and between John Snow (physician) and Henry Whitehead (reverend), the source of London's 1854 cholera outbreak is chased down to a single public water pump on Broad Street.

title: Hiking Trails in Bookston Bay
author: Val Bomier
description: Get lost and find yourself amidst the stunning natural beauty of Bookston Bay's secret hiking trails. Stunning coastal vistas await around every corner!

title: Into the Sunset: The Magical West
author: Cemal M. Fahmy
description: Explore the mythical and exotic lands of Western Europe. This satirical travelogue lets you in on the secret wisdom and mysterious culture of the West.

title: My Travels In East Africa
author: Tao Ryota
description: From Burundi to Uganda, an ageing adventurer shares his eye-opening journey through Eastern Africa, learning life's greatest lessons along the way.

title: The Secret History of Bookstonbury
author: H. A. Pennington
description: An insight into the forgotten anecdotes of history, which was hugely popular in 1953 and still makes for an entertaining read. However, most of these historical "theories" have since been disproven.

title: The Secret Island; The Secret Series #1
author: Enid Blyton
description: A cozy tale of four children, Mike, Peggy, Nora and their friend Jack, who escape to a "secret" island on a serene lake, where they live an unfettered life of stowing away in a willow-treehouse and foraging for their own food.

title: Selected Stories of Anton Chekhov
author: A. Chekhov, L. Volokhonsky & R. Pevear
description: 30 stories from the Russian writer and playwright, famous for his painterly prose and use of foreshadowing. This collection features The Huntsman , A Boring Story , The Lady with the Little Dog (a crowd-pleaser), and Chekhov's personal favourite, The Student .

title: Hélène
author: St. Bookston
description: A romantic reinterpretation of the Illiad. Hélène, a 16th-century version of Helen of Troy, has the chance to forever change the trajectory of her life and love. A historical play and a St. Bookston classic for a reason!

title: Hello Lighthouse
author: Sophie Blackall
description: A Caldecott Award Winning picture book, Say hello to a lighthouse keeper and his wife, guarding the coast through the days of stormy waves and sunny skies, waiting for the arrival of their child. At the end, wave goodbye to the lighthouse on their return to the mainland.

title: A Collection of Poems
author: St. Bookston
description: A collection of Saint Bookston's greatest works of poetry, including Ashen Grey , Prometheus' Regrets , and Last Breaths .

title: A Senseless Power
author: St. Bookston
description: A timeless family drama by the brilliant Bookston. The three sons of a rich merchant family are vying for their powerful mother's approval. Will their quest for the matriarch's position be worth the destruction they sow on their ways to the top?

title: On the Naturale Flora of Bookstonborough
author: St. Bookston
description: A taxonomy of the flora of Bookston Bay from the late 16th century. With hand-drawn illustrations by the polymath Saint Bookston.

title: Rebecca
author: Daphne du Maurier
description: Our protagonist is freshly married to a rich manor lord. At her new home, expectations of a carefree married life are shattered when questions about Rebecca, the late lady of the house, arise.

title: Carmilla
author: J. Sheridan Le Fanu
description: The lesbian vampire story you didn't know you needed! This classic gothic horror novel details young Laura's encounter with a new guest at her father's castle, a young woman named Carmilla.

title: Anne of Green Gables
author: L.M. Montgomery
description: Anne of Green Gables is the redheaded and feisty orphan girl you can't help but love! This charming children's classic is beloved by readers of all ages around the world.

title: Guards! Guards!
