author: Terry Pratchett
description: If you're looking to get into the Discworld series, this 8th tale is the one to start with. (There's a lot of them!) Adventure awaits the magical lands of Ankh-Morpork, when a long-lost "noble" dragon suddenly returns and is promptly crowned King.

title: The Haunting of Hill House
author: Shirley Jackson
description: In this tense horror classic, a group surrounding an "expert of the occult" are investigating the mysterious Hill House. But inside, they are awaited by more than just spooky poltergeists...

title: Dinosaurs and other Prehistoric Life
author: Anusuya Chinsamy-Turan
description: A collection of over 90 prehistoric plants and animals, stunningly illustrated by Angela Rizza and Daniel Long. In this remarkable guide, readers of all ages may find their new favourite fossil!

title: Newtonian Physics for Babies
author: Chris Ferrie
description: This book is the only physics guide truly written for everyone! Whether you are only months old or already retired, this cheeky picture book might make a genius out of you yet.

title: The Adventures of Pippi Longstocking
author: Astrid Lindgren
description: Follow the energetic escapades of young Pippi, the girl with the red braids who lives all alone in her big colourful house with her trusty pet monkey always at her side, and who doesn't listen to what the boring adults have to say.

title: Codename Villanelle
author: Luke Jennings
description: An assassin going by the codename "Villanelle" has recently appeared on the map, killing some of the most influential men in international politics. Can former MI6 agent Eve find and catch this eccentric psychopath?

title: Coffee First, Then the World
author: Jenny Graham
description: We've all been on a bike, maybe even done a few long-distance rides. But Jenny Graham took it much further: She cycled around the world! This is her raw, unfiltered, and hilarious account of how she became the fastest woman to ever circumnavigate the globe on two wheels.

title: Moominland Midwinter
author: Tove Jansson
description: The Moomins are lovable small creatures, invented by the Finnish illustrator, who live a peaceful life in the forest. In the 8th book of the classic children's series, little Moomintroll wakes up during winter hibernation and has to be very brave about it.

title: The Witch Boy
author: Molly Knox Ostertag
description: In Aster's family, boys aren't meant to be witches, they're supposed to grow into shapeshifters. But at 13, Aster still hasn't shifted, and when his friends need help, his fascination with witchcraft might be the only thing that can help. A graphic novel for adventurous middle-grade readers.

title: The Bookshop Book
author: Lucy Mangan
description: Part memoir, part love letter to children’s literature, you will revisit childhood favourites and likely find gems you missed the first time round. Ideally, read wrapped in a blanket and in a window seat if at all possible.

title: Borne
author: Jeff VanderMeer
description: In a post-apocalyptic city, climate refugee Rachel adopts a surreal creature. The creature's questions hold a mirror to humanity, reflecting back the good, the bad, and the absurd. But is Borne as innocent as they seem, or merely a quiet, growing threat?

title: Bookworm; A Memoir of Childhood Reading
author: Jen Campbell
description: Get a glimpse into the most unusual bookshops around the world and fall in love with their proprietor's passion for the trade. I might be biased, but if you ask me, this love letter to weird and wonderful bookshops is only missing one entry (*chrm* yours truly *chrm*).

title: What We Don't Talk About; When We Talk About Fat
author: Aubrey Gordon
description: This revolutionary book aims to challenge the cultural attitudes and systemic biases behind anti-fatness and calls for a social justice movement that includes fat activism.

title: Witch Hat Atelier; Volume 1
author: Kamome Shirahama
description: How can Coco ever become a witch if she was born without the gift of magic? Well, a mysterious magician might hold the missing puzzle pieces for her dreams to come true! This popular manga series promises loveable characters and a whole lot of magic.

title: The Surgeon
author: Tess Gerritsen
description: A sadistic serial killer is on the loose in Boston, and evidence of his surgical skills leads investigator Rizzoli to suspect that he might be a physician. A dark and twisted thriller and the first in the popular Rizzoli & Isles crime series.

title: The Taking of Annie Thorne
author: C.J Tudor
description: Joe Thorne has never gotten over his sister's disappearance and her unsettling return. As Stephen King says ( and surely Joe would agree , "sometimes, dead is better". Now he's home, back where it all went wrong, seeking answers and revenge as he confronts the past.

title: Tasting History; Explore the Past through 4,000 Years of Recipes
author: Max Miller
description: Have you ever wondered what people were cooking during the Great Depression? Or did you always want to try a recipe from Ancient Rome? Max Miller was curious about the same thing, and this fun book recreates his viral cooking adventures for the page.

title: Happily Ever After Cookbook; Original Recipes for Book Lovers
author: Various Authors
description: Book-inspired recipes! Need I say more? When bestselling romance authors team up with chefs to create their own dishes, you might be in for a treat! Try it at home!

title: Cook As You Are; Recipes for Real Life, Hungry Cooks and Messy Kitchens
author: Ruby Tandoh
description: Sometimes, our lives just don't leave space for cooking. Or do they? These delicious recipes work for all kinds of situations, whether you need last-minute inspiration, only have one clean pot, or can't easily chop ingredients.

title: Cook Korean!; A Comic Book with Recipes
author: Robin Ha
description: Most people like having visual aids in their recipes. But this book takes illustrated cooking to the next level! Enjoy this colourful and fun guide to Korean cuisine, and make cooking new recipes more fun than ever.

title: A Cook's Tour; Global Adventures in Extreme Cuisines
author: Anthony Bourdain
description: Experience global culinary adventures with beloved chef Anthony Bourdain! A savoury travel memoir in search of the perfect meal.

title: The Stonewall Reader
author: The New York Public Library
description: This curated anthology chronicles the Stonewall uprisings after fifty years through articles, first accounts, and more. Iconic activists and forgotten revolutionaries, who were indispensable to the gay liberation movement, tell their stories.

title: We Are Bridges; A Memoir
author: Cassandra Lane
description: To come to terms with a new stage in her life, Cassandra explores what that family memory means to her. She carries on a tradition of Black Women's storytelling and history-keeping to contrast her present day with the South in the early 20th century.

title: We Solve Murders; Book 1
author: Richard Osman
description: Amy is working as a bodyguard for a famous author on her private island when a body washes onshore. Thankfully, her father-in-law, Steve, is a retired police officer with plenty of free time on his hands! The first case in a series for this dynamic duo.

title: Hawaii's Story by Hawaii's Queen
author: Lili'uokalani
description: Queen Lili'uokalani was the last reigning monarch of Hawai'i, before the kingdom was overthrown and annexed as a territory of the United States of America. A unique and informative autobiography.

title: Heartless
author: Marissa Meyer
description: Not all fairytales have a happy ending. The Queen of Hearts is a brutal monarch. But once, she was just Catherine - young and idealistic. Shenanigans ensue when Cath meets Jest, sparking a forbidden love story where hearts are stolen, broken and freely given...

title: Botany in a Day; The Patterns Method of Plant Identification
author: Thomas J. Elpel
description: Want to impress your friends and family with this great plant identification party trick? This book covers more than 100 plant families and how to spot their common features. Become a botany expert!

title: The Boundless Sea; A Human History of the Oceans
author: David Abulafia
description: In this dauntingly comprehensive volume, explore humankind's relationship with the planet's greatest body of water - the ocean. This definitive work chronicles the world history of maritime empires and trade routes; while debunking long-held myths and beliefs.

title: Boy's Life
author: Robert R. McCammon
description: When a boy and his father witness the aftermath of a gruesome murder, their lives become haunted by paranoia. The boy is forced to grow up quickly in a town where every friendly face becomes a potential murderer.

title: The Boy, The Mole, The Fox and The Horse; (Book 1)
author: Charlie Mackesy
description: In a world where we have to navigate so much, unlikely friends often help us find our way home. So goes for the boy, the mole, the fox, and the horse, who share their life lessons along the way. With beautiful watercolour pictures, this is truly a book for all ages!

title: Boys run the riot, Vol. 1
author: Keito Gaku
description: Ryo, a trans teen fed up with gender rules (especially skirts), finds freedom in fashion. Teaming up with a rebellious classmate, they start a clothing brand to express themselves beyond labels. A bold, queer and stylish manga about self-acceptance and friendship.

title: Boys run the riot, Vol. 1
author: Keito Gaku
description: In volume two of this heartfelt manga, trans teen Ryo and rebel Jin have launched their DIY fashion brand Boys Run the Riot, but Ryo struggles with coming out. Can he stay true to himself and still make it in fashion?

title: Breakfast at Tiffany's
author: Truman Capote
description: Holly Golightly might seem shallow and carefree, with her many suitors and piles of gifts. But as the young writer gets to know her-first out of curiosity, then attraction - he realises she's not cheap, she's priceless .

title: The Bright Sword
author: Lev Grossman
description: The adventure of Collum and the oddballs of the Round Table as they seek to restore order to the kingdom after the death of King Arthur and the heroes of legend. Together, they will learn the troubled past of King Arthur and mysteries of Britain.

title: British Boutique Hotels
author: Gina Jackson
description: From quiet country retreats to luxurious city stays, this pocket-sized guide is your key to Britain's best boutique hotels! A highly opinionated and indispensable companion for the discerning traveler.

title: Brown Girl Dreaming
author: Jacqueline Woodson
description: An award-winning memoir-in-verse. Jacqueline uses poetry to share what it was like growing up Black during the 1960s-1970s in South Carolina and New York, including the growing joy she found in writing. A powerful, yet approachable book for middle-grade readers.

title: The Bullet That Missed; A Thursday Murder Club Mystery #3
author: Richard Osman
description: Another week at Copper's Chase retirement village, another cold case for Joyce, Elizabeth, Ibrahim, and Ron to solve. A stranger from Elizabeth's past arrives to threaten her, but the Thursday Murder Club always keep their confidences and protects their own!

title: Bury Our Bones in the Midnight Soil
author: V.E. Schwab
description: A sensual slow burn about immortal love and what drives us to obsession. Dark, sapphic, beautiful vampires. Yes please.

title: A Buzz in the Meadows; The Natural History of a French Farm
author: Dave Goulson
description: A tale of how Goulson transformed a derelict farm into a sanctuary for plants and pollinators. Filled with humorous anecdotes and fascinating science, this book is a heartfelt plea to cherish and protect life in all its forms—especially the tiniest of creatures.

title: Entangled Life; How Fungi Make Our Worlds, Change Our Minds & Shape Our Futures
author: Merlin Sheldrake
description: They can make us healthy, make us sick, make us drunk or high, or grow on our graves once we are gone. Merlin Sheldrake (what a great name) lets us in on the secrets of the fungi, the coolest lifeform on Earth.

title: Escape from Mr. Lemoncello's Library; Mr. Lemoncello's Library #1
author: Chris Grabenstein
description: Kyle Keeley never met a puzzle he didn't like. So he's thrilled when a famous game maker invites him and 12 other kids to an overnight lock-in, the grand opening of the town library. In the morning, the doors are still locked. Solve the puzzles and escape the library!

title: The Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
description: Charles Darwin's groundbreaking research on natural selection became one of the founding texts of modern biology and science. His discoveries were used to argue against a creationist belief system and created the grounds for a new study of evolution.

title: Provence to Pondicherry; Recipes from France and Faraway
author: Tessa Kiros
description: Starting in Provence and following the routes of early French explorers, Kiros takes us on a  journey to discover French culinary influences in far-flung colonial destinations through an array of delicious recipes.

title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
author: Becky Chambers
description: In a beautifully futuristic world running on solar power and mutual aid, our protagonist, Dex, lives a very fulfilling life as a monk. Still, something is missing in their life, and something calls them on a journey into the wilderness.

title: Pygmalion
author: George Bernard Shaw
description: Professor Henry Higgins bets he can coach a socially awkward flower seller into passing as an aristocratic lady. He doesn't expect to fall in love with her. This humorous play pokes fun at classicism in the 10th century, and was later adapted as the musical My Fair Lady .

title: A Raisin in the Sun
author: Lorraine Hansberry
description: The youngers, a Black family in 1950s Chicago, await an insurance payment that could radically improve their circumstances but can't agree on how to spend it. A play about the barriers of upward mobility, housing discrimination, and the pressures to assimilate.

title: The Royal Horticultural Society Encyclopedia of Gardening
author: Royal Horticultural Society
description: With this reference work, it is easier than ever to pick up gardening! Simply follow the guides, made easy with the help of over 3000 photographs, or look up any questions you might have about your plants. Guaranteed green thumb!

title: The Ruins of Gorlan; (Ranger's Apprentice #1)
author: John Flanagan
description: Rangers are mysterious figures, believed to practice strange magic. But when young Will is chosen to become a Ranger's apprentice, he discovers a whole new world of secrets. And on the horizon, a fierce enemy wakes...

title: Russians in Alaska, 1732-1867
author: Lydia T. Black
description: A comprehensive overview of a time when Alaska was once Russian. The harsh exploitation of people, natural resources, socioeconomic factors, and the complexity of relationships formed from this time are covered in this definitive work.

title: Annihilation
author: Jeff VanderMeer
description: Why has every previous expedition into Area X ended in a horrible tragedy? And what actually hides inside the contaminated zone? Four scientists are sent to find out in this first volume of a tense cosmic horror trilogy.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: An emotionally-charged Russian novel about love triangles, affairs, and farming. Wish you could be the hero of your own tragic story? Ride a sad train with Anna Karenina.

title: The Fisherman
author: John Langan
description: It begins as a slow, melancholy tale of two widowed fishermen in upstate New York. But this unusual horror epic quickly turns into a deeply moving and intimate nightmare that will leave you awake at night.

title: The Sea Around Us
author: Rachel Carson
description: An incredible insight into the history of our oceans, their influence and power, but also their fragility, written by American marine biologist and conservationist Rachel Carson.

title: The Sea Inside
author: Philip Hoare
description: A collection of anecdotes, histories, and mythologies from Philip's seemingly aimless wanderings across the world - each one, in its own way, connected to the sea, its islands, and its maritime creatures.

title: Spirals in Time; The Secret Life and Curious Afterlife of Seashells
author: Helen Scales
description: Helen Scales has the perfect name for a marine biologist and wrote the perfect book for all of us who are fascinated by members of the phylum Mollusca. Explore the history of these curious sea creatures with shells.

title: Spring Clean
author: Sabreen Islam
description: A soft and touching poetry collection, exploring memories both painful and nostalgic. Teaches readers the importance of a spring clean, making space to reflect on the past to see a brighter future.

title: The Search; Avatar The Last Airbender (#4-6)
author: Konietzko, DiMartino & Yang
description: Finally find out what happened to Zuko's and Azula's mother in this continuation of the animated series! Aang and his friends are once again saddled up on their flying bison and are hurdled straight into another emotional and hilarious adventure.

title: Wake; The Hidden History of Women-Led Slave Revolts
author: Rebecca Hall & Hugo Martínez
description: This revolutionary graphic novel uncovers the history of women who fought for their freedom on slave ships and throughout the Americas. It is a powerful exploration of resistance at the intersection of white supremacy and patriarchy.

title: The Magic Fish
author: Trung Le Nguyen
description: An emotional yet hopeful YA graphic novel about the son of Vietnamese immigrants. His parents struggle with their English, so how can Tien really talk to them about what he is going through? Will they understand when he tells them he is gay?

title: An Age of License; A Travelogue (#1)
author: Lucy Knisley
description: This comic is many things: a charming travel memoir about a trip through Europe, a lighthearted advice book for anyone with travel anxieties, and a book full of beautiful illustrations of cute kittens and delicious food.

title: An Atlas of Countries that Don't Exist
author: Nick Middleton
description: From vast regions like Catalonia to tiny islands claimed by a single person, this book tours 50 unrecognised and largely unnoticed 'countries' - by turns hilarious, heartbreaking, and fascinating. The perfect bunny-slipper read for the armchair traveler

title: An Experiment with an Air Pump
author: Shelagh Stephenson
description: On the cusp of a new century, deep in the throes of scientific discovery, one house has concealed a secret for 200 years; a literal body in the basement! This play jumps between the past and present, examining scientific ethics and dramatics.

title: This Was Our Pact
author: Ryan Andrews
description: No one turns for home. No one looks back. That's the promise Ben and his friends made as they set our to follow the paper lanterns go. Eventually it's only Ben and Nathaniel on a delightfully weird and magical journey in this stunning graphic novel.

title: Thornhill
author: Pam Smy
description: Mary is an orphan living at the Thornhill Institute, who tells her story in her diary. Ella, whose story is told through artful comic strips, has just moved into a street with an old, abandoned house... A dark and haunted story fit for young readers!

title: Three Bags Full; Sheep Detective Story #1
author: Leonie Swann & Anthea Bell
description: A humorous murder mystery set on a hillside near Glennkill, Ireland. A flock of sheep are outraged that someone got away with murdering their shepherd, George. Can this eclectic cast of sheep detectives figure out who killed him? An absolutely baaa-tty first book.

title: Thumbelina
author: Hans Christian Andersen
description: Born from a flower, tiny Thumbelina drifts past marriage-minded toads, moles, and bossy swallows, trying to find a home where she's loved, not used. A sweet fairy tale about finding where you belong.

title: Troglobites Don't Bite
author: Mayara Ferreira
description: What does life look like in total darkness? It's much more busy than you would think! Get to know the most fascinating cave-dwellers: from worms to snails, spiders, crustaceans, insects, fish, amphibians, and even the occasional mammalian visitor!

title: How Many Castles in 7 Days?
author: Stephen Jezek
description: Stephen is a fan of castles, and he always manages to visit one wherever he travels. On his effective quest to see the most castles in only one week, Stephen compares the Czech Republic, Thuringia, and Wales in this hilarious travelogue.

title: How to Stop Time
author: Matt Haig
description: Discover immortality as it has never been explored before. A historical fantasy about finding yourself, and learning how to live by the hand of Tom Hazzard, who has been alive for barely 400 years.

title: Dragon Ball; Volume 1
author: Akira Toriyama
description: The most energetic and funny adventure awaits young manga fans in this classic series. Join the super-strong Goku on a fantastical quest for the seven Dragon Balls that have the power to grant wishes!

title: Dragonology; The Complete Book of Dragons
author: Ernest Drake
description: Dr Drake's quintessential guide for any budding dragonologist. Learn how to identify different dragon species, understand their biology, and live peaceably alongside them. Contains maps, specimens, and secret messages to spark the imagination!

title: Jujutsu Kaisen; Volume 1
author: Gege Akutami
description: Supernatural strength, cursed objects, and occult research are becoming daily occurrences for Yuji Itadori, the high school outcast protagonist of this popular manga series. A dark adventure for teen readers!

title: Ranma 1/2; Volume 1
author: Rumiko Takahashi
description: All that the teenager Ranma Saotome wants to do is train in martial arts. But a cursed spring queers his pitch, so to speak, because now, every time he is splashed with water, he changes into a girl. The beginning of a sweet and romantic manga series.

title: Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint; Volume 1
author: singNsong & UMI
description: This epic manwha series brings a whole new twist on the reverse-isekai trope! Dokja Kim is the only reader of an obscure online novel. So when the dystopic events of the story suddenly occur in real life, he might be the only one who can still rewrite fate!

title: On the Banks of Plum Creek; (Little House, Book 4)
author: Laura Ingalls Wilder
description: Laura and her family leave their house on the prairie for Plum Creek in Minnesota. During the day, Laura and Mary go to school, do chores, and go fishing. At night, Pa's fiddle sings them to sleep. Fourth in a classic series perfect for little pioneers!

title: Sailor Moon; Volume 1
author: Naoko Takeuchi
description: You know her, you love her: Usagi Tsuniko might be a bit sensitive and clumsy, but when her friends are in trouble, she turns into THE magical girl and protector of all teenage girls. Join Sailor Moon and her talking cat in her sweet and romantic manga adventures!

title: Ouran High School Host Club; Volume 1
author: Bisco Hatori
description: What awaits Haruhi, the poor girl at an expensive private school, when she suddenly has to work off a debt to some weird all-male after-school club? Well, first of all, she has to dress the part... A quirky and hilarious romance manga for young adults.

title: My Lesbian Experience With Loneliness
author: Nagata Kabi
description: A very candid memoir in which the author shares her journey with mental health, sexuality, and growing up. A must-read for josei fans!

title: Monster; Volume 1
author: Naoki Urasawa
description: The brilliant surgeon Dr Kenzo Tenma might be the only one who can find out the twisted motivations of a cold and calculating serial killer, in this tense and dark crime thriller in manga form.

title: The Rose of Versailles
author: Riyoko Ikeda
description: This shojo manga is a historical romance classic. Alongside Marie Antoinette's life at Versailles and the brewing unrest among the French, we follow Lady Oscar, a noblewoman who lives as a man so she can command the palace guard.

title: FAKE; Volume 1
author: Sanami Matoh
description: When Ryo becomes a detective in New York, he is partnered up with the American Dee, who soon reveals his feelings for Ryo. Fake is a lighthearted romantic comedy series for all BL manga fans with 90s nostalgia.

title: Dickens at Christmas
author: Charles Dickens
description: Bah! Humbug! A collection of Dickens' famous Christmas tales, both heartwarming and spooky. This edition includes A Christmas Carol, The Chimes, A Cricket on the Hearth, Battle of Life, and the Haunted Man.
